docs.title: Vergil Actions
docs.text: Shared GitHub Actions library providing reusable composite actions for CI/CD across all managed repositories.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Stable (v2.x) — Actions and reusable workflows are consumed by pinning to a rolling minor tag (e.g., @v2.1), which automatically receives patch releases.

docs.title: Action categories
docs.text: Phase Actions Purpose CI / Security codeql, semgrep SAST scanning CI / Version Bump version-divergence Pre-merge version validation CI / Matrix matrix Per-version job matrix and container images CI / Evidence emit Per-gate CI evidence artifact CD / Release tag-and-release Release tagging and GitHub Releases CD / Release validate-inputs, ci-evidence-gate, registry-publish, ci-evidence-attach cd-release input checks, pre-publish evidence gate, build and registry publish, post-publish evidence attach CD / Docs deploy MkDocs Material + mike versioned deployment Ops / GitHub Config branch-sweep Delete branches whose PR is merged or closed Shared / Security trivy Vulnerability scanning and SBOM generation Shared / Docs stage Stage changelog and release-notes pages for the docs build Shared / Setup vergil, system-packages, build-command vergil-tooling install and CI version set; test-job system packages and build command Package setup Package toolchain for package build and install-test containers Local freeze-internal-refs Pin this repository's internal action refs to the release tag (used only by its own cd.yml)

docs.title: Reusable workflows
docs.text: Reusable workflows provide canonical job and check names across all managed repositories. See Reusable Workflows for details.

docs.title: CI (pre-merge)
docs.text: Workflow Purpose ci-docs Strict MkDocs build of the documentation site ci-security Security scanning (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep) ci-quality Common linting, custom validation, language-specific lint and typecheck ci-audit Dependency audit ci-test Unit tests ci-version-bump Version divergence gate ci-package Build and install-test .deb/.rpm packages (repos with [package] only)

docs.title: CD (post-merge)
docs.text: Workflow Purpose cd-release Full release pipeline (tag, build, publish, version bump), plus signed .deb/.rpm packages for repos with [package] cd-docs MkDocs documentation deployment cd-docs-refresh Regenerate a docs site's generated pages (roadmap, activity) and redeploy it; the caller runs it on a schedule and on demand publish-index Signed apt/dnf package-repository site for an <org>/packages repo, deployed to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• Composite actions only — No custom JavaScript or Docker actions. Every action is a composite action.yml with shell steps.
  • Reusable workflows — CI and CD workflows are provided as reusable workflow_call templates that produce canonical check names across all consuming repositories.
  • Self-referencing CI — This repository's own CI uses ./actions/... and ./.github/workflows/... local paths, so changes are tested by the same PR that modifies them.
  • Centralized standards — Workflow patterns and validation rules are defined once here and consumed by all repositories.

docs.title: Canonical standards
docs.text: This repository follows the vergil-tooling repository for commit messages, branching, versioning, and code management practices.

docs.title: Repository Configuration
docs.text: This page documents the GitHub configuration prerequisites that each managed repository needs before CI workflows, automation, and project integration work correctly. For action-specific configuration (inputs, outputs, behavior), see the Action Reference.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Each repository requires specific secrets depending on its workflow set. Secrets are configured in Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions.

Secret Required by Purpose PROJECT_TOKEN All repositories Adds new issues to the GitHub Project via the add-to-project workflow APP_CLIENT_ID Every repository with an ops.yml or epic-rollup.yml, and [package] repositories Client ID of the org's automation GitHub App (<org>-automation) APP_PRIVATE_KEY Every repository with an ops.yml or epic-rollup.yml, and [package] repositories Private key of the org's automation GitHub App

docs.title: PROJECT_TOKEN
docs.text:
A classic personal access token (PAT) that grants the add-to-project workflow permission to add issues to a user-owned GitHub Project.

Required scopes: project, repo

Why a classic PAT? Fine-grained personal access tokens do not support user-owned Projects v2. The GitHub Projects v2 GraphQL API requires a classic token with the project scope.

Creation steps:

  1. Go to Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Tokens (classic).
  2. Click Generate new token (classic).
  3. Set a descriptive name (e.g., add-to-project automation).
  4. Select scopes: project (full control) and repo (full control).
  5. Generate the token and copy it immediately.
  6. Set the secret in each repository:
gh secret set PROJECT_TOKEN --repo vergil-project/<repo> --body "<token>"

Do not pipe tokens via stdin

Always use the --body flag when setting secrets with gh secret set. Piping the token via stdin (printf '%s' 'TOKEN' | gh secret set ...) can corrupt the secret value during encryption, causing "Bad credentials" errors at runtime that are difficult to diagnose.

docs.title: APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY
docs.text:
These secrets hold the Client ID and private key of the org's automation GitHub App. Workflows pass them to actions/create-github-app-token to mint a short-lived installation token for work that GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do.

Each org has its own automation App, named <org>-automation. The App is owned by the org (registered under the org's Developer settings, not a personal account), and its installation covers all repositories in that org:

Org App vergil-project vergil-project-automation logical-minds-foundry logical-minds-foundry-automation mnemosys-project mnemosys-project-automation

The App is an automation identity, not a per-contributor one. It is separate from the per-developer agent Apps described in vergil-tooling's Identity Architecture.

Why a GitHub App? A reusable workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN can carry only the permissions its caller grants, and the standard ops.yml grants just contents: read and issues: write. It is also limited to the repository the run belongs to. The App token supplies the extra scopes (for example Dependabot alerts or branch deletion) and the cross-repository reach (the org's .github epics, the org's packages index) these workflows need.

Who uses it. Every repository with an ops.yml needs these secrets, not only library repositories:

Workflow Job or step Token scope ops-github-config.yml branch-sweep, github-config, dependabot-audit Calling repository only ops-epic-rollup.yml epic-rollup (from the caller's epic-rollup.yml) Calling repository and the epic repository ops-epic-sweep.yml epic-sweep Every repository the App is installed on in the org ops-upstream-refresh.yml upstream-refresh Calling repository only cd-release.yml Package-index dispatch <org>/packages only

App permissions required. The table lists what each consumer needs, which is the minimum the App must hold. Read the App's actual permission set from its settings page before relying on it:

Permission Access Needed by Metadata Read-only Required by GitHub (always enabled) Administration Read-only github-config: vrg-github-repo-config audit reads repository settings, branch protection, rulesets, Actions permissions and whether vulnerability alerts are enabled Contents Read & write branch-sweep (deletes branch refs); upstream-refresh (pushes the upstream-refresh branch, and deletes it when it closes a stale refresh PR); cd-release.yml package-index dispatch to <org>/packages; github-config reads vergil.toml and the CI workflow Pull requests Read & write upstream-refresh (opens, updates, comments on and closes the refresh PR); branch-sweep reads them (decides which branches are finished) Issues Read & write ops-epic-rollup.yml and ops-epic-sweep.yml (close, relabel and link issues) Dependabot alerts Read-only dependabot-audit (vrg-dependabot-audit lists open alerts)

Administration stays read-only. The Apps run only the read-only vrg-github-repo-config audit. vrg-github-repo-config apply, which changes settings and rulesets, is a human action that runs as the maintainer's own gh login, never as the App. Do not grant Administration: Read & write.

vergil-actions' own release workflow (cd.yml) also uses the vergil-project-automation App token for its checkout, because the release tag it pushes points at the freeze-internal-refs commit, which changes workflow files. That needs Workflows: Read & write (see local/freeze-internal-refs). That is specific to this repository; consumer workflows do not need it.

Creation steps:

  1. Go to the org's Settings > Developer settings > GitHub Apps, so the App is owned by the org.
  2. Click New GitHub App.
  3. Name it <org>-automation and set the homepage URL.
  4. Under Permissions > Repository permissions, grant the permissions listed above.
  5. Disable webhooks (not needed).
  6. Create the app and note the Client ID from the app's settings page.
  7. Under Private keys, click Generate a private key. Save the downloaded .pem file.
  8. Under Install App, install it on the org and choose All repositories.
  9. Make APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY available to every repository that calls the workflows above. For example, as repository secrets:
gh secret set APP_CLIENT_ID --repo <org>/<repo> --body "<client-id>"
gh secret set APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo <org>/<repo> --body "$(cat <path-to-private-key>.pem)"

Changing a permission later:

  1. On the App's settings page, open Permissions & events, change the permission and save.
  2. Accept the change on the installation: Org settings > GitHub Apps > \ > Configure, then review and accept the pending permission request. GitHub does not apply a new App permission to an installation until it is accepted, and until then minted tokens do not carry it. For Dependabot alerts, the dependabot-audit job exits 2 ("could not check") on every repository and the ops run fails.

    Key rotation: Generate a new private key from the app's settings page, update the APP_PRIVATE_KEY secret wherever it is stored for that org, then revoke the old key. Each org has its own App and key, so rotate per org.

docs.title: Binary package environments
docs.text:
Repositories whose vergil.toml has a [package] section, and the organization's <org>/packages index repository, keep their signing key in GitHub environments (Settings > Environments), not in repository secrets. Each environment's deployment-branch policy restricts it to a single branch.

Environment Repository Admits Secrets Used by package-signing Each [package] repository main only PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY, PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE The package-sign job in cd-release.yml index-signing <org>/packages develop only PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY, PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE The build-index job in publish-index.yml

PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY holds the ASCII-armored export of the org signing subkey. index-signing admits develop because repository_dispatch and schedule runs always use the default branch.

Environment secrets reach these cross-repo reusable workflows only when the caller passes secrets: inherit. An explicit secrets: map leaves them empty (vergil-project/packages#6). See Release publishing secrets.

The GitHub App behind APP_CLIENT_ID / APP_PRIVATE_KEY must also be installed on <org>/packages with Contents: Read & write, so that cd-release.yml can dispatch package-released to it after a packaged release.

docs.title: Container system packages
docs.text: A repository can declare extra Debian packages under [container].system-packages in its vergil.toml. On CI, the ci-test workflow installs those packages on its test jobs (via the shared/setup/system-packages action), so tests run against the same system dependencies as the local dev container. The key's schema and semantics are documented on the vergil-tooling side: container-config reference.

docs.title: Container build command
docs.text: A repository can declare a build step under [container].build-command in its vergil.toml. On CI, the ci-test workflow runs that command on its test jobs (via the shared/setup/build-command action, after the system-packages install and before the tests), so tests run against the same build output as the local dev container. The step fails closed with no retry — a failing build command fails the test job immediately rather than being retried. After it runs, the action exports NODE_PATH so a node library the build baked out-of-workspace resolves; note that NODE_PATH is honoured by CommonJS require only and ignored by ESM import. The key's schema and semantics are documented on the vergil-tooling side: container-config reference.

docs.title: GitHub Project integration
docs.text:
The add-to-project workflow automatically adds new issues to a GitHub Project when they are opened. Each repository has an add-to-project.yml workflow that references a project URL and uses the PROJECT_TOKEN secret.

- uses: actions/add-to-project@v1.0.2
  with:
    project-url: https://github.com/users/<owner>/projects/<number>
    github-token: ${{ secrets.PROJECT_TOKEN }}

The project-url value varies by repository — repositories may belong to different projects. This is configured directly in the workflow file, not as a secret.

docs.title: Repository rulesets
docs.text:
Every managed repository uses three rulesets to enforce merge requirements:

  • Branch protection — PR requirements for main and develop
  • CI gates — Required status checks for main and develop
  • Tag protection — Protect semver release tags (v*.*.*); allow rolling minor tags

For detailed configuration including settings, check names per repository type, and API commands, see Repository Rulesets.

docs.title: Workflow permissions
docs.text: GitHub Actions workflows use the GITHUB_TOKEN for most operations. This token is automatically created per workflow run and scoped to the repository.

docs.title: Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions
docs.text:
Each workflow declares its minimum required permissions at the top level:

permissions:
  contents: read
Permission Typical workflows contents: read CI (test, lint, validate) contents: write Documentation deployment, publish (tagging) security-events: write CodeQL, Semgrep, Trivy (SARIF upload) attestations: write Build provenance attestation (Python, Java) id-token: write OIDC-based publishing (PyPI trusted publisher) pull-requests: write Publish workflow (version bump PR creation)

docs.title: When external tokens are needed
docs.text:
The GITHUB_TOKEN is insufficient in two cases:

  1. GitHub Project access — The GITHUB_TOKEN cannot interact with user-owned Projects v2. The PROJECT_TOKEN (classic PAT) is required.
  2. Scopes and repositories beyond the caller's grant — a reusable workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN carries only what the caller grants and reaches only its own repository. The org's automation App token (APP_CLIENT_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY) is required for the nightly ops jobs (config audit, branch sweep, Dependabot alert audit), the epic roll-up and sweep, and the package-index dispatch. See APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY.

docs.title: Auto-merge
docs.text:
All managed repositories have auto-merge enabled in repository settings. This allows PRs to merge automatically once all required status checks pass.

To enable: Settings > General > Pull Requests > Allow auto-merge.

docs.title: New repository onboarding checklist
docs.text: Use this checklist when adding a new repository to the managed environment.

docs.title: 1. Repository settings
docs.text:
• [ ] Set default branch to develop
  • [ ] Enable auto-merge (Settings > General > Pull Requests)
  • [ ] Enable Automatically delete head branches

docs.title: 2. Rulesets
docs.text:
Create three rulesets per the standard configuration:

  • [ ] Branch protection — targeting main and develop (details)
  • [ ] CI gates — targeting main and develop with required checks (details)
  • [ ] Tag protection — targeting v*.*.* with admin bypass (details)

Use explicit branch references

Always use refs/heads/main and refs/heads/develop in ruleset conditions. Never use ~DEFAULT_BRANCH — it resolves to develop (the default branch), silently leaving main unprotected. See Branch targeting.

docs.title: 3. Secrets
docs.text:
• [ ] Set PROJECT_TOKEN (all repositories)
  • [ ] Make APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY for the org's automation App available to the repository (every repository with an ops.yml, not only libraries)
gh secret set PROJECT_TOKEN --repo vergil-project/<repo> --body "<token>"
gh secret set APP_CLIENT_ID --repo vergil-project/<repo> --body "<client-id>"
gh secret set APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo vergil-project/<repo> --body "$(cat <key>.pem)"

docs.title: 4. GitHub App installation
docs.text:
• [ ] Confirm the org's <org>-automation App installation has All repositories access, so it already covers the new repository (Org settings > GitHub Apps > \ > Configure). There is no per-repository install step.
  • [ ] Verify by checking Settings > GitHub Apps on the repository
  • [ ] After the first nightly ops run, confirm the dependabot-audit job did not exit 2 ("could not check")

docs.title: 4a. Binary packages ([package] repositories only)
docs.text:
See Binary package environments.

  • [ ] Create a package-signing environment whose deployment-branch policy admits only main
  • [ ] Add PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE to it
  • [ ] Call cd-release.yml with secrets: inherit # nosemgrep: yaml.github-actions.security.secrets-inherit.secrets-inherit
  • [ ] Call ci-package.yml under a job keyed package and add package / evidence to the CI gates ruleset

For the <org>/packages index repository itself:

  • [ ] Create an index-signing environment that admits only develop, holding PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE
  • [ ] Set Settings > Pages > Source to GitHub Actions
  • [ ] Call publish-index.yml with secrets: inherit (same nosemgrep comment)

docs.title: 5. Workflow files
docs.text:
• [ ] Add add-to-project.yml with the correct project URL
  • [ ] Add ci.yml with standard checks for the repository type
  • [ ] Add cd.yml with docs and/or release jobs as needed

docs.title: 6. CI gates activation
docs.text:
• [ ] Push the CI workflow and verify all checks run
  • [ ] Add each check name to the CI gates ruleset (procedure)

docs.title: 7. Verification
docs.text:
• [ ] Open a test issue and confirm it appears in the GitHub Project
  • [ ] Open a test PR and confirm all required checks run
  • [ ] Confirm auto-merge works after checks pass

docs.title: Consuming actions
docs.text:
Reference actions from this repository using the full path with a rolling minor tag pin:

uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/<action-path>@v2.1

Tag pinning

Pin to a rolling minor tag (e.g., @v2.1) to automatically receive patch releases. Pin to an exact tag (e.g., @v2.1.1) for full reproducibility.

docs.title: Minimal workflow example
docs.text:
name: CI - Test and Validate

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  codeql:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
        with:
          language: python

docs.title: Consuming reusable workflows
docs.text:
Reusable workflows produce canonical check names across all repositories. Reference workflows using the full path to the workflow file:

uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1

docs.title: CI workflow example
docs.text:
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: python

docs.title: CD workflow example
docs.text:
name: CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [develop, main]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  docs:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-docs.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: write

  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
    # Python publishes via OIDC trusted publishing — no secret to pass.

docs.title: Release publishing secrets
docs.text:
A repo without a [package] section in vergil.toml must forward only the publishing credentials the target ecosystem needs, never a blanket secrets: inherit. The generated cd.yml emits an explicit secrets: block (or none at all) matching the language:

Ecosystem Secrets to forward python None — OIDC trusted publishing (requires id-token: write) go None rust CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN java CENTRAL_USERNAME, CENTRAL_TOKEN, GPG_PRIVATE_KEY, GPG_PASSPHRASE

For example, a Rust release job forwards a single least-privilege secret:

  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: rust
    secrets:
      CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}

A repo with a [package] section (one that publishes .deb/.rpm binary packages) is the exception: it must pass secrets: inherit. Its package-sign job reads PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE from the repo's main-only package-signing environment, and environment secrets reach a cross-repo reusable workflow only through secrets: inherit. An explicit secrets: map does not deliver them, so the signing key arrives empty and package-sign fails (verified by a controlled probe, vergil-project/packages#6). inherit also forwards APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY, which the release uses to dispatch the package index. Semgrep's secrets-inherit rule flags the line, so suppress it there with the rule ID:

  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: rust
    # Required for [package] repos: environment secrets (package-signing)
    # only reach the reusable workflow with inherit.
    secrets: inherit  # nosemgrep: yaml.github-actions.security.secrets-inherit.secrets-inherit

See CD Release: binary packages for the package-signing environment and the GitHub App setup.

See Reusable Workflows for the full list and detailed documentation.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Each action documents its required workflow permissions. Common patterns:

Permission Actions that require it contents: read All actions (repository checkout) contents: write docs-deploy, publish/tag-and-release security-events: write security/codeql, security/semgrep, security/trivy

docs.title: Self-referencing CI
docs.text:
This repository uses local paths (./actions/...) rather than remote references in its own CI workflow. This means changes to an action are validated by the same PR that modifies them — no separate integration testing step is needed.

Consuming repositories use the full remote reference (vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/...@v2.1).

docs.title: Action Reference
docs.text: All actions are composite GitHub Actions located under the actions/ directory, organized by pipeline phase. Each action is self-contained with an action.yml definition and optional supporting scripts.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
• ci/security/codeql — Runs GitHub CodeQL static analysis for a single language.
  • ci/security/semgrep — Runs Semgrep SAST scanning with language-specific and cross-cutting security rulesets.
  • ci/version-bump/version-divergence — Verifies that the PR branch version differs from the main branch version.
  • ci/matrix — Builds the per-version job matrix (version label and container image for each entry) from the resolver outputs of shared/setup/vergil; auto-wired into ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test.
  • ci/toolchain/pin-python — Pins uv to a Python leg's resolved version and to the image's interpreter (UV_PYTHON, UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system); auto-wired into the Python matrix legs of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test.
  • ci/toolchain/assert — Fails a CI leg whose running Python or Go is not the version CI resolved for it; auto-wired into the matrix legs of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test.
  • ci/evidence/emit — Writes a gate's evidence.json and uploads it with the gate's report files as a ci-evidence-<gate> artifact for the release-time evidence bundle.

docs.title: CD
docs.text:
• cd/release/tag-and-release — Creates annotated git tags and GitHub Releases.
  • cd/release/validate-inputs — Checks the cd-release inputs and fails early on an invalid combination.
  • cd/release/ci-evidence-gate — Pre-publish gate: harvests the release PR's CI evidence artifacts and checks they are complete before anything is published.
  • cd/release/registry-publish — Builds the release for the repository's language ecosystem, attests it, generates an SBOM and, when enabled, publishes to the package registry.
  • cd/release/ci-evidence-attach — Post-publish: assembles the evidence bundle including the SBOM, attests it and attaches it to the GitHub Release.
  • cd/docs/deploy — Deploys MkDocs documentation using mike for versioned documentation.

docs.title: Ops
docs.text: • ops/github-config/branch-sweep — Deletes branches whose PR is merged or closed and lists them in the job summary, flagging merged-PR leftovers (auto-wired into ops-github-config).

docs.title: Shared
docs.text:
• shared/security/trivy — Runs Trivy vulnerability scanning, SBOM generation, or container image scanning.
  • shared/docs/stage — Stages the changelog and release-notes pages and patches the MkDocs nav, so ci-docs and cd-docs build from the same source tree.
  • shared/setup/vergil — Installs the vergil-tooling version pinned in vergil.toml and resolves the CI version set with vrg-ci-resolve (versions, primary-version, primary-container-tag, container-tags, container-suffixes; auto-wired into the reusable workflows).
  • shared/setup/primary-suffix — Picks a single-container job's image suffix from the resolver's primary version, with the caller's container-suffix as a must-match cross-check (auto-wired into ci-quality, ci-version-bump and cd-release).
  • shared/setup/system-packages — Installs a repository's declared [container].system-packages on CI test jobs (test-runtime only; auto-wired into ci-test).
  • shared/setup/build-command — Runs a repository's declared [container].build-command on CI test jobs (test-runtime only; auto-wired into ci-test; fail-closed with no retry; exports NODE_PATH so a baked out-of-workspace node library resolves).

docs.title: Package
docs.text: • package/setup — Installs the package toolchain in a package build or install-test container: OS prerequisites (apt mirror list on x86_64 Ubuntu, fail-fast apt, a single apt-get update), a pinned uv, vergil-tooling, and nFPM.

docs.title: Local
docs.text:
Actions used only by this repository's own workflows, not by consumers.

  • local/freeze-internal-refs — Rewrites this repository's relative ./actions/... and @develop refs to absolute refs at the release tag, checks none remain and commits the result (used by cd.yml).

docs.title: docs-deploy
docs.text: Deploys MkDocs documentation using mike for versioned documentation. Handles git configuration, version detection, and mike deploy/set-default.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/docs/deploy@v2.1
  with:
    version-command: cat VERSION | cut -d. -f1,2
    mkdocs-config: docs/site/mkdocs.yml
    mike-command: mike

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description version-command Yes — Shell command to extract the version string on main (e.g. cat VERSION, grep -oP ... version.go). mkdocs-config No docs/site/mkdocs.yml Path to mkdocs.yml configuration file. mike-command No mike Command to run mike. Set to uv run mike for Python repos that manage their own dependencies via their project's virtual environment.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: • contents: write (required for pushing to the gh-pages branch)

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Configure git identity — Sets the git user to github-actions[bot] for the deploy commit. Marks the workspace as a safe directory to avoid dubious-ownership errors in container jobs.
  2. Determine version — On main, runs the version-command to extract the version and sets alias=latest. On all other branches, sets version=dev with no alias.
  3. Stage changelog and release notes — Copies CHANGELOG.md and releases/*.md into the docs directory, and generates a release notes index page sorted by semver. Uses system Python (/usr/local/bin/python3) to avoid venv PATH shadowing.
  4. Patch mkdocs nav — Injects release version entries into the mkdocs.yml nav under the Releases section.
  5. Deploy docs — On main, runs mike deploy --push --update-aliases <version> latest followed by mike set-default --push latest. On other branches, runs mike deploy --push dev.

docs.title: Reusable workflow
docs.text:
Docs deployment is typically consumed via the cd-docs.yml reusable workflow rather than calling the composite action directly:

jobs:
  docs:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-docs.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: write

docs.title: Interpreter source
docs.text: The action's "Deploy docs" step sets UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system, and the cd-docs.yml docs job sets it in its job env too, so it also reaches the pre-deploy command. For Python repositories, uv run mike and uv run mkdocs then use the image's Python, never a managed Python that uv downloads because the repository sets python-preference = "only-managed". If the image cannot satisfy the repository's requires-python, the deploy fails loudly. Only the source is pinned: UV_PYTHON is not set (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec §6.5; issue #1002). The pin is on the step, so a direct caller of this action gets it without setting anything.

docs.title: MkDocs 2.0 banner
docs.text: The cd-docs.yml workflow sets NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING=1 on its "Deploy docs" step, which reaches the mkdocs and mike processes this action starts. Without it, mkdocs-material 9.7.x prints a MkDocs 2.0 warning banner on every build. Callers of cd-docs.yml cannot set it, because a caller's env does not reach a reusable workflow. The workflow sets the variable, not the action, so to hide the banner when you call the action directly, set it in that step's env. The variable only hides the banner. Consumers still pin mkdocs<2 in their own docs dependencies. Added in v2.1.43 (#947, PR #948).

docs.title: Direct usage (standalone)
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/docs/deploy@v2.1
  with:
    version-command: cat VERSION | cut -d. -f1,2

docs.title: Python repo with uv-managed dependencies
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/docs/deploy@v2.1
  with:
    version-command: cat VERSION | cut -d. -f1,2
    mike-command: uv run mike

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text:
• GitHub Pages — Enable GitHub Pages in repository settings with source set to Deploy from a branch and branch set to gh-pages.
  • The gh-pages branch is created automatically by mike deploy --push on first run.

docs.title: cd/release/ci-evidence-attach
docs.text:
The post-publish CI-evidence step. It assembles the evidence bundle from what cd/release/ci-evidence-gate downloaded, adds the SBOM built earlier in the job, attests the bundle, and attaches it to the GitHub Release. It runs after tag-and-release, because both the Release (the upload target) and the SBOM (bundle content) exist only then.

This action is wired automatically into the cd-release release job. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves; they choose the mode with the cd-release input evidence-enforce.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Attach CI evidence bundle (post-release)
  id: evidence_attach
  continue-on-error: ${{ !inputs.evidence-enforce }}
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/ci-evidence-attach@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    enforce: ${{ inputs.evidence-enforce }}
    sbom-file: ${{ steps.evidence_sbom.outputs.path }}

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH and the .ci-evidence-staging directory that ci-evidence-gate left in the workspace earlier in the same job.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 2.1.129). tag Yes — Release tag the bundle is attached to (e.g. v2.1.129). enforce No "true" "true" (enforcing): a bundling or upload failure fails the step. "false" (warning): it emits a ::warning:: and the step succeeds. Warning mode is a temporary opt-out, not a permanent soft gate. timeout-minutes No "15" Upper bound on the assemble step, enforced with the coreutils timeout command. A timeout counts as a bundling failure. sbom-file No "" Path to the SBOM that registry-publish built. Included when the file exists; when it is set but missing, the step logs a notice and bundles without it.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description attached "true" only when the bundle was assembled, attested and uploaded to the Release. Empty on any failure, in either mode.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Assemble. Runs vrg-ci-evidence assemble with --staging .ci-evidence-staging, the version, a UTC --generated-at timestamp and --sbom-file when the SBOM exists. The command makes no network calls: it builds the tarball and a standalone manifest in evidence-out/ from the evidence already downloaded. On failure it reports failed (exit <rc>) or timed out after <n>m and exits with that code in enforcing mode, or 0 with a warning in warning mode.
  2. Attest. Runs actions/attest-build-provenance on evidence-out/*.tar.gz. Skipped when assembly failed.
  3. Attach. Runs gh release upload <tag> evidence-out/*.tar.gz evidence-out/*-manifest.json --clobber and writes attached=true on success. A failed upload is fatal in enforcing mode and a warning in warning mode. Skipped when assembly failed.

The attest step is a uses: step, so the shell's warning-mode handling cannot catch its failure. cd-release covers that with continue-on-error: ${{ !inputs.evidence-enforce }} on the calling step.

docs.title: Enforcement in cd-release
docs.text: A plain Enforce CI evidence attach step follows this one and, in enforcing mode, fails the job when the attach step's outcome is failure or it succeeded without attached=true (#925). By then the tag and Release are already published, so its error says the release is missing its evidence bundle and needs operator attention.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• contents: write (to upload Release assets)
  • id-token: write and attestations: write (for the provenance attestation)

docs.title: cd/release/ci-evidence-gate
docs.text:
The pre-publish CI-evidence gate. It finds the release PR, downloads the ci-evidence-<gate> artifacts its CI produced (see ci/evidence/emit), and checks that every required gate's evidence is present and complete. It runs before anything is published, so in enforcing mode no package, tag or Release is created without complete evidence.

It does not build, attest or attach anything: at this point the GitHub Release does not exist and the SBOM is not built. cd/release/ci-evidence-attach does that after tag-and-release, from the evidence this action downloaded.

This action is wired automatically into the cd-release release job. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves; they choose the mode with the cd-release input evidence-enforce.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: CI evidence gate (pre-publish)
  id: evidence_gate
  continue-on-error: ${{ !inputs.evidence-enforce }}
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/ci-evidence-gate@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    enforce: ${{ inputs.evidence-enforce }}

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 2.1.129). enforce No "true" "true" (enforcing): a failure or timeout fails the step, before publish. "false" (warning): it emits a ::warning:: and the step succeeds. Warning mode is a temporary opt-out, not a permanent soft gate. timeout-minutes No "15" Upper bound on the harvest, enforced with the coreutils timeout command (composite steps cannot use timeout-minutes). A timeout counts as a gate failure.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description passed "true" only when the harvest exited 0. Empty on any failure or timeout, in either mode.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The action runs one step:

timeout "${TIMEOUT_MINUTES}m" vrg-ci-evidence harvest \
  --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --merge-sha "$GITHUB_SHA" \
  --out-dir "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.ci-evidence-staging"

vrg-ci-evidence harvest resolves the release PR from the merge commit, downloads the required gate artifacts, validates them, and exits non-zero when a required gate is missing or incomplete. It leaves the downloaded evidence and a harvest-state.json in .ci-evidence-staging, which ci-evidence-attach reads later, so the artifacts are downloaded once.

On success the step writes passed=true. On failure it reports failed (exit <rc>) or timed out after <n>m, then exits with the tool's code in enforcing mode, or exits 0 with a warning in warning mode.

docs.title: Enforcement in cd-release
docs.text: cd-release does not rely on the step's exit code alone. A plain Enforce CI evidence gate step follows it and fails the job when, in enforcing mode, the gate step's outcome is failure or it succeeded without passed=true. So a gate failure cannot be masked into a green step (#925). See All Hard Gates.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• actions: read, to list and download the release PR's ci-evidence-* artifacts from its CI run. A reusable workflow's permissions are capped by the caller, so the consuming repository's cd.yml must grant it too.
  • contents: read (the cd-release release job grants contents: write for its other steps).

The step authenticates with the workflow's github.token.

docs.title: cd/release/registry-publish
docs.text:
Builds the release for the repository's language ecosystem, optionally attests the build and generates an SBOM, and, when enabled, publishes to the package registry. Build and publish commands come from vergil-tooling's ecosystem metadata (vrg-ecosystem-resolve) unless the caller overrides them.

This action is wired automatically into the cd-release release job, where its Build and publish step runs for python, java, rust and go repositories. Consuming repositories set its behavior through the cd-release inputs and secrets, not by calling it directly.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Build and publish
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/registry-publish@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    registry-publish: "true"
    attestation-subject-path: dist/*
    sbom-output-file: sbom-$VERSION.cdx.json

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description language Yes — Primary language. Selects the ecosystem build and publish commands. version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 1.2.3). Exported as VERSION to the build and publish commands. registry-publish No "false" "true" runs the publish step. build-command No "" Replaces the ecosystem build command. publish-command No "" Replaces the ecosystem publish command. attestation-subject-path No "" Glob of build outputs to attest with actions/attest-build-provenance. Empty skips attestation. sbom-output-file No "" SBOM output path; $VERSION is replaced with the version. Empty skips the SBOM. cargo-registry-token No "" Rust: crates.io token. Exported as CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, which cargo publish reads. central-username No "" Java: Maven Central username. Exported as MAVEN_USERNAME. central-token No "" Java: Maven Central token. Exported as MAVEN_PASSWORD. gpg-private-key No "" Java: GPG signing key. gpg-passphrase No "" Java: GPG passphrase. Exported as MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE, which maven-gpg-plugin reads.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description build-command The build command used (derived or overridden). publish-command The publish command used (derived or overridden). sbom-output-file The SBOM path with $VERSION replaced; empty when no SBOM was requested.

docs.title: Ecosystem commands
docs.text:
The derived commands come from vergil-tooling's language registry:

Language Build Publish Credential variable python uv build uv publish none (PyPI trusted publishing) java ./mvnw package -B ./mvnw deploy -B MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE rust cargo build --release cargo publish CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN go go build ./... none none

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Derive commands. Runs vrg-ecosystem-resolve <language>, which sets build, publish and credential-secret step outputs, then replaces build or publish with build-command / publish-command when given. An unsupported language fails the step.
  2. Configure Maven credentials (java only). Writes ~/.m2/settings.xml with a central server that reads MAVEN_USERNAME / MAVEN_PASSWORD, and imports gpg-private-key when set.
  3. Resolve version placeholders. Replaces $VERSION in sbom-output-file.
  4. Build. Creates dist/, then runs the build command with VERSION set. Skipped when there is no build command.
  5. Attest build provenance. Runs actions/attest-build-provenance on attestation-subject-path. Skipped when it is empty.
  6. Generate SBOM. Runs shared/security/trivy with scan-type: sbom. Skipped when sbom-output-file is empty.
  7. Publish. Runs only when registry-publish is "true" and there is a publish command. The step sets CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, MAVEN_USERNAME, MAVEN_PASSWORD and MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE from the inputs, then runs publish.sh. When the ecosystem names a credential variable and that variable is empty, the step fails with an ::error:: naming the cd-release secret to set (or telling you to turn registry-publish off): CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN comes from the CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret and MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE from the GPG_PASSPHRASE secret. A requested publish that cannot happen never lets the release report success. A credential variable this action does not set also fails the step, since it means vergil-tooling and vergil-actions disagree on the name. Python names no credential: uv publish uses PyPI trusted publishing, which needs id-token: write and a trusted publisher configured for the project on PyPI.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• contents: read to build
  • id-token: write and attestations: write when attestation-subject-path is set
  • id-token: write to publish a python release (PyPI trusted publishing)

docs.title: cd/release/tag-and-release
docs.text:
Creates an annotated git tag, a develop changelog boundary tag, and a GitHub Release. All mutating steps are skipped when the tag already exists, making the action safe to re-run.

Rolling minor tags

Rolling minor tags (e.g. v1.2) are no longer created by this action. They are now managed by vrg-promote in the release orchestrator's promote phase.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/tag-and-release@v2.1
  with:
    version: "1.2.3"
    release-title: mqrestadmin
    release-notes: "Release notes markdown here"
    release-artifacts: ""
    tag-prefix: v

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 1.2.3). release-title Yes — Release title prefix (e.g. mqrestadmin, pymqrest). release-notes Yes — Full markdown body for the GitHub Release. release-artifacts No "" Space-separated glob of files to attach to the GitHub Release. Leave empty for no artifacts. tag-prefix No v Prefix prepended to the version to form the git tag.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Name Description tag The full tag name that was (or would be) created (e.g. v1.2.3). tag-created true if a new tag was created, false if it already existed.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: • contents: write (required for creating tags and releases)

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Compute tag name — Concatenates tag-prefix and version (e.g. v + 1.2.3 = v1.2.3).
  2. Check existing tag — If the tag already exists, all subsequent steps are skipped (idempotent re-run).
  3. Configure git identity — Sets the git user to github-actions[bot].
  4. Create annotated tag — Creates and pushes v<version> with message Release <version>.
  5. Tag develop for changelog boundaries — Fetches develop and creates a develop-v<version> tag pointing at origin/develop, then pushes it. This enables changelog generation between releases.
  6. Create GitHub Release — Uses gh release create with the provided title, notes, and optional artifacts.

docs.title: Standard library release
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/tag-and-release@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    release-title: mqrestadmin
    release-notes: ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.notes }}

docs.title: Release with build artifacts
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/tag-and-release@v2.1
  with:
    version: "2.0.0"
    release-title: myapp
    release-notes: "## What's New\n\nInitial v2 release."
    release-artifacts: "dist/*.tar.gz dist/*.whl"

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text: • Branch protection — The GITHUB_TOKEN must have permission to push tags. If tag protection rules are configured, ensure the workflow token is allowed.

docs.title: cd/release/validate-inputs
docs.text:
Checks the cd-release inputs before anything else runs and fails early on an invalid combination. It runs vrg-release-validate-inputs from vergil-tooling.

This action is wired automatically as the first check in the cd-release release job. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Validate inputs
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/validate-inputs@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    container-tag: ""
    registry-publish: "true"

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description language No "" The repository's language. Empty for repositories with no language ecosystem. container-tag No "" Container image tag. cd-release passes the release job's tag, the resolver's primary-container-tag from its setup job, never a caller input. registry-publish No "false" Whether publishing to a package registry is enabled ("true" to enable).

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The step fails when either of these holds for a language vergil-tooling supports:

  • registry-publish is "true" but the language has no publish command (e.g. go, cpp, typescript).
  • container-tag is set but the language is not one of python, java, rust or go.

It passes without checking when language is empty. A language that vergil-tooling does not support also passes: the action hands the language to vrg-release-validate-inputs as a positional argument, and the tool rejects an unsupported language only when it is given with --language.

docs.title: ci/evidence/emit
docs.text:
Writes a gate's evidence.json and uploads it, with the gate's report files, as a ci-evidence-<gate> workflow-run artifact. At release time cd-release harvests these artifacts (vrg-ci-evidence) into the attested evidence bundle it attaches to the GitHub Release (see cd/release/ci-evidence-gate and cd/release/ci-evidence-attach).

This action is wired automatically into the evidence-producing jobs of the reusable CI workflows:

Workflow gate ci-security security ci-quality quality ci-audit audit ci-test test ci-package package

Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/evidence/emit@v2.1
  with:
    gate: test
    files: |
      evidence-reports/coverage-*.xml
      evidence-reports/junit-*.xml
    tools: '[{"name": "pytest"}, {"name": "coverage.py"}]'

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description gate Yes — Evidence gate name: security, test, audit, quality or package. Sets the artifact name (ci-evidence-<gate>) and the gate field of evidence.json. files No "" Newline- or space-separated report file paths or globs to include (e.g. SARIF, coverage XML, JUnit XML). An entry that matches no file is skipped, not an error. tools No [] JSON array for the tools field, e.g. [{"name":"codeql","version":"2.17.0"}]. metrics No {} JSON object for the metrics field, e.g. coverage percent or finding counts.

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Stage. Creates $RUNNER_TEMP/ci-evidence-<gate>, copies every regular file that matches an entry in files into it (flattened to its basename), and writes evidence.json:

    {"gate": "<gate>", "tools": [...], "metrics": {...}, "files": ["<basename>", ...]}

    tools and metrics must be valid JSON; jq fails the step otherwise. 2. Upload. Uploads the staging directory as the ci-evidence-<gate> artifact with actions/upload-artifact.

Because evidence.json is always written, the artifact is always produced, even for a gate that has no report files yet. Whether an artifact is complete enough is decided at release time: the harvest rejects an evidence.json-only payload as incomplete (see All Hard Gates).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: None beyond the default; uploading a workflow artifact needs no extra scope.

docs.title: ci/matrix
docs.text:
Builds the per-version job matrix for a reusable CI workflow. Each matrix entry carries the version label, used in the job and check name, and the fully qualified container image the leg runs in.

The versions, and the image suffix and tag of each, come from the single resolver, vrg-ci-resolve, by way of the outputs of shared/setup/vergil. This action does no version or family routing of its own.

This action is wired automatically into the matrix job of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Install vergil-tooling
  id: setup
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/vergil@v2.1

- name: Resolve matrix
  id: resolve
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/matrix@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    versions: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.versions }}
    primary-version: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.primary-version }}
    container-tags: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.container-tags }}
    container-suffixes: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.container-suffixes }}
    container-suffix: python

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description language Yes — Primary language of the calling repository (e.g. python, cpp, shell). Selects the run-once collapse only. versions Yes — The setup action's versions output, e.g. ["3.14","3.13"] or ["clang-20","gcc-14"]. primary-version Yes — The setup action's primary-version output. container-tags Yes — The setup action's container-tags output: version to image tag. container-suffixes Yes — The setup action's container-suffixes output: version to image suffix. container-prefix No prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev). container-suffix No "" The calling workflow's container-suffix, used only as a cross-check. When set, it must be one of the resolved suffixes.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description all JSON array of {version, image} objects, one per resolved version. Used by per-version kinds (TEST always; TYPECHECK for C++ and the single-suffix languages). once The primary version's entry alone for C++ and TypeScript; identical to all for every other language. Used by run-once kinds (LINT and AUDIT; TYPECHECK too for TypeScript).

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Every image is ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<container-suffixes[v]>:<container-tags[v]>, for every language:

Version Resolver's suffix and tag Image clang-20 cpp-clang, 20 prod-cpp-clang:20 gcc-14 cpp-gcc, 14 prod-cpp-gcc:14 node-24 ts-node, 24 prod-ts-node:24 3.14 python, 3.14 prod-python:3.14 latest (no language) base, latest prod-base:latest

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
The action fails with an ::error:: annotation, and writes no matrix, when:

  • an input is empty, or versions is not a non-empty JSON array;
  • a version has no tag in container-tags or no suffix in container-suffixes;
  • primary-version is not one of versions;
  • container-suffix is set but is not one of the resolved suffixes. The workflow's inputs and the repository's vergil.toml then disagree on the language (for example container-suffix: python with no [project].primary-language, which resolves to prod-base:latest), and the legs would run on the wrong image.

docs.title: Run-once kinds
docs.text: For C++ and TypeScript some check kinds run once, on the primary version, rather than once per version: LINT and AUDIT for C++; LINT, AUDIT and TYPECHECK for TypeScript. The once output gives those jobs a one-entry matrix.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The logic is in resolve.sh next to action.yml, so it can be unit tested (tests/resolve.test.sh). The step prints both resolved arrays to the job log. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

docs.title: security/codeql
docs.text: Runs GitHub CodeQL static analysis (init + autobuild + analyze) for a single language.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    queries: "+security-extended"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description language Yes — CodeQL language to analyze (e.g. python, javascript, go, java). queries No +security-extended Query suite to run.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• security-events: write (required for uploading SARIF results)
  • contents: read

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Initialize CodeQL — Uses github/codeql-action/init@v4 to set up the CodeQL database for the specified language and query suite.
  2. Autobuild — Uses github/codeql-action/autobuild@v4 to automatically detect and build the project.
  3. Run analysis — Uses github/codeql-action/analyze@v4 to perform the analysis and upload results. Results are categorized by /language:<language>.

docs.title: Python CodeQL analysis
docs.text:
jobs:
  codeql:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
        with:
          language: python

docs.title: Go CodeQL analysis
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
  with:
    language: go

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text:
• GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) — Must be enabled on the repository for SARIF upload to work. For public repositories, GHAS is available by default. For private repositories, a GHAS license is required.
  • Code scanning alerts — Results appear in the repository's Security > Code scanning alerts tab.

docs.title: security/semgrep
docs.text: Runs Semgrep static analysis with language-specific and cross-cutting security rulesets.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/semgrep@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    extra-config: "p/owasp-top-ten"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description language Yes — Language ruleset to enable (maps to p/<language>, e.g. python, java, golang). extra-config No "" Additional Semgrep config strings, space-separated (e.g. p/owasp-top-ten). upload-sarif No true Upload SARIF to GitHub code scanning (a copy with accepted-suppressed results removed by vrg-sarif-filter; requires vergil-tooling on PATH). Set to false on private repos without GHAS; results are attached as a build artifact instead.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• security-events: write (required for uploading SARIF results)
  • actions: read (required by the SARIF upload on private repositories)
  • contents: read

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Check language ruleset — Queries the Semgrep registry to verify that p/<language> exists. If the registry does not have a ruleset for the specified language, the language-specific config is silently skipped.
  2. Auto-detect rulesets — Scans the repository for content that benefits from specialized rulesets:
    • p/dockerfile — enabled when Dockerfile* files are present
    • p/github-actions — enabled when .github/workflows/ contains workflow files
  3. Run scan — Executes semgrep scan with the following config rulesets:
    • p/ci — CI pipeline security rules (injection, secrets in workflows, unsafe patterns)
    • p/command-injection — Unsafe shell construction and command injection patterns
    • p/security-audit — Cross-cutting security audit rules
    • p/secrets — Secret detection rules
    • p/<language> — Language-specific rules (if available in the registry)
    • p/dockerfile — Dockerfile best practices (if Dockerfiles detected)
    • p/github-actions — GitHub Actions injection patterns (if workflow files detected)
    • Any additional rulesets from extra-config
  4. Filter and upload SARIF — Runs vrg-sarif-filter to write semgrep-results.upload.sarif, a copy with accepted-suppressed results (e.g. justified nosemgrep) removed, and uploads that copy to GitHub code scanning using github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v4, categorized as semgrep. The unfiltered semgrep-results.sarif is left in place for the evidence bundle. These steps run even if the scan finds issues (if: always()) and need vergil-tooling on PATH. When upload-sarif is false, the SARIF file is attached to the workflow run as a build artifact (semgrep-sarif) instead.

docs.title: Rule exclusions
docs.text: The underlying vrg-semgrep-scan supports a repeatable --exclude-rule <full-rule-id> flag that drops individual findings by their full Semgrep rule ID. Caller-supplied --exclude-rule values are added on top of the fleet DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_RULES — they never replace the defaults, so the fleet baseline always applies.

docs.title: Fleet default: github-actions-mutable-action-tag
docs.text:
github-actions-mutable-action-tag is currently exempted fleet-wide (it lives in DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_RULES). This rule flags third-party actions pinned to a mutable tag (e.g. @v4) rather than a full commit SHA. The exemption is temporary, pending backlog vergil-project/.github#194 — once pin-advancement tooling exists to keep SHA pins current, third-party action SHAs will be pinned and the exemption lifted.

Our own vergil-project/vergil-actions/…@v2.1 references are a permanent exception: they track our controlled release line and are never SHA-pinned, so the rule does not apply to them regardless of the backlog above.

docs.title: Python Semgrep scan
docs.text:
jobs:
  semgrep:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/semgrep@v2.1
        with:
          language: python

docs.title: Go with additional OWASP rules
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/semgrep@v2.1
  with:
    language: golang
    extra-config: "p/owasp-top-ten"

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text:
• GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) — Must be enabled for SARIF upload. On private repos without GHAS, set upload-sarif: false to preserve results as a build artifact instead.
  • Code scanning alerts — Results appear in the repository's Security > Code scanning alerts tab alongside CodeQL results.

docs.title: Future rulesets
docs.text: Additional Semgrep rulesets (such as p/owasp-top-ten for web application security) can be enabled per-repo via the extra-config input. These are not included in the base config because they target specific application types that not all repos in the fleet share.

docs.title: ci/toolchain/assert
docs.text:
Fails a CI leg when the interpreter or toolchain actually running it is not the version CI resolved for it. A repository's own files can choose the interpreter behind Vergil's back (for Python, .python-version or uv's python-preference), and a leg would then pass on a version it never ran. This action is the backstop for that.

This action is wired automatically into every matrix leg of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test, as the assert-toolchain step. It runs after the dependency install. For Python, an earlier step in the leg (ci/toolchain/pin-python) sets UV_PYTHON to the leg's version and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE to only-system, so uv uses the image's interpreter for the install and the checks. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: assert-toolchain
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/toolchain/assert@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    expected: ${{ matrix.version }}

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description language Yes — Primary language of the calling repository. expected Yes — The version CI resolved for this leg, as x.y (e.g. 3.14, 1.26). Ignored for languages without an assertion.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Language Check python Runs uv run --frozen python -c '...' and compares the interpreter's x.y with expected, logging the interpreter's path. --frozen keeps uv from rewriting uv.lock. go Runs go env GOVERSION in the module (so a toolchain switch in go.mod is what gets reported) and compares its x.y (go1.26.3 is 1.26). Any other No check yet; prints a ::notice:: saying so and passes.

On a mismatch the step fails with ::error::CI resolved <expected> but the job runs <actual>. It also fails, with an ::error:: annotation, when expected is not an x.y version or the toolchain cannot be asked for its version.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The logic is in assert.sh next to action.yml, so it can be unit tested (tests/assert.test.sh, which fakes uv and go). The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• shared/setup/vergil — resolves the versions the legs run.
  • ci/matrix — builds the legs from those versions.

docs.title: ci/toolchain/pin-python
docs.text:
Pins uv to a CI leg's Python interpreter. It exports two variables to the rest of the job:

Variable Value What it fixes UV_PYTHON The leg's resolved x.y The version: the one CI resolved, not one a repository file such as .python-version selects. UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE only-system The source: the image's interpreter.

A repository may set uv's python-preference (for example only-managed, so a local VM never seeds a venv from the host interpreter). That setting picks managed versus system Python, not the version. Without the second variable, a leg in such a repository would have uv download its own managed Python and pass on an interpreter the image never provided. With it, uv always uses the image's interpreter, and a missing interpreter fails the leg instead of being downloaded (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec §6.5). uv's environment variables take precedence over a repository's uv settings.

This action is wired automatically into every Python matrix leg of ci-quality (lint, typecheck), ci-audit (dependencies) and ci-test (unit), and into ci-quality's single-container custom job (on the primary version), before the dependency install. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves. ci/toolchain/assert is the backstop that checks the result.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Pin uv to the leg's Python interpreter
  if: inputs.language == 'python'
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/toolchain/pin-python@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ matrix.version }}

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description version Yes — The Python version CI resolved for this leg, as x.y (e.g. 3.14).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: Appends UV_PYTHON=<version> and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system to $GITHUB_ENV. The step fails with an ::error:: annotation, writing nothing, when version is not an x.y version or GITHUB_ENV is not set.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
The logic is in pin.sh next to action.yml, so it can be unit tested (tests/pin.test.sh). The same harness also checks the CI workflows: every job with an assert-toolchain step must pin through this action, and no workflow may set UV_PYTHON by hand. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

The harness also guards the interpreter source everywhere uv runs against a repository's project (issue #1002). Every workflow job that runs a uv project command (uv run, uv sync, uv lock and so on) or uses ci/toolchain/assert must pin UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system before that point: through this action, or with a job-level env. Jobs that resolve no version, such as the ci-docs and cd-docs docs jobs, use the job env. Every composite action or script that runs one must pin it on the step's env or inline on the command line. There are two exceptions:

  • ci/toolchain/assert is pinned by its caller.
  • package/setup/detect.sh reads vergil.toml in raw package-build images that ship no Python, so it needs uv's managed interpreter. Instead of the pin, every uv command in it must pass --no-config, so the repository's uv settings cannot reach it at all (issue #1003). Without it, a repository that sets python-downloads = "manual" stops uv downloading that interpreter.

uv tool commands are not checked, because uv ignores a project's uv settings for them. Fixture workflows and actions test the guard both ways.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ci/toolchain/assert — fails the leg if it runs a version other than the resolved one.
  • ci/matrix — builds the legs and their versions.

docs.title: release-gates/version-divergence
docs.text: Verifies that the PR branch version differs from the main branch version. Fails the step if the two versions are identical.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/version-bump/version-divergence@v2.1
  with:
    head-version-command: cat VERSION
    main-version-command: git show origin/main:VERSION

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description head-version-command Yes — Shell command that prints the HEAD (PR branch) version to stdout. main-version-command Yes — Shell command that prints the main branch version to stdout.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Name Description head-version The version extracted from the PR branch. main-version The version extracted from the main branch. diverged true if versions differ, false otherwise.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: • contents: read (default)

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Fetch main branch — Runs git fetch origin main --depth=1.
  2. Compare versions — Executes both version commands and compares the results. If the versions are identical, the step fails with exit code 1 and a diagnostic message. If they differ, the step succeeds.

docs.title: Simple VERSION file check
docs.text:
jobs:
  version-gate:
    name: "release: version-divergence"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/version-bump/version-divergence@v2.1
        with:
          head-version-command: cat VERSION
          main-version-command: git show origin/main:VERSION

docs.title: Python project version check
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/version-bump/version-divergence@v2.1
  with:
    head-version-command: >-
      grep -oP 'version\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' pyproject.toml
    main-version-command: >-
      git show origin/main:pyproject.toml | grep -oP 'version\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+'

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text: • Required status check — Add this as a required status check on the develop branch to prevent PRs from merging without a version bump.

docs.title: local/freeze-internal-refs
docs.text:
Rewrites this repository's internal action and workflow refs to absolute refs at the release tag, checks that none are left unfrozen, and commits the result. It runs vrg-freeze-refs from vergil-tooling.

This is a local action: only this repository's own cd.yml uses it, in the release job on main, just before cd/release/tag-and-release. It is not meant for consuming repositories.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: During development the workflows and actions here refer to each other with relative refs (./actions/..., ./.github/workflows/...) or @develop, so a PR is tested by the code it changes. A consumer that pins @v2.1.0 must get the actions from that same release, and a relative ref does not resolve when a reusable workflow is called from another repository. Freezing the refs at release time solves both. See Reference freezing.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Freeze internal refs to release tag
  uses: ./actions/local/freeze-internal-refs
  with:
    tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}

- name: Tag and release
  uses: ./actions/cd/release/tag-and-release
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description tag Yes — Release tag to freeze to (e.g. v1.5.20). owner-repo No ${{ github.repository }} OWNER/REPO used to build the absolute refs.

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Configure the git identity as github-actions[bot].

  2. Freeze and validate. Runs vrg-freeze-refs --owner-repo <owner-repo> --tag <tag> over every .yml and .yaml file under .github/workflows and actions. On each line that contains uses: it rewrites:

    From To ./actions/<path> <owner-repo>/actions/<path>@<tag> ./.github/workflows/<path> <owner-repo>/.github/workflows/<path>@<tag> <owner-repo>/<path>@develop <owner-repo>/<path>@<tag>

    It then fails the step, listing each line in the job summary, if any relative or @develop ref remains. 3. Commit. If anything changed, stages .github/workflows and actions and commits chore(release): freeze internal refs to <tag>.

The commit is not pushed to a branch. The tag-and-release step that follows tags HEAD, so the frozen refs exist only at the release tag; develop and main keep their relative refs.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The step itself only edits and commits locally. Because it changes files under .github/workflows, cd.yml checks out with a GitHub App token that has workflows: write: GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push a tag whose commit changes workflow files.

docs.title: ops/github-config/branch-sweep
docs.text:
Deletes the branches on a repo whose pull-request work is finished, and lists every deleted branch in the job summary. It runs vrg-branch-sweep --apply from vergil-tooling, which decides what counts as finished and what is never deleted.

This action is the scheduled safety net behind the delete-on-merge repo setting and the delete-on-close rule. It is wired automatically into the branch-sweep job of the ops-github-config.yml reusable workflow, so every repo whose ops.yml calls that workflow is swept on the same nightly schedule as its config audit. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ops/github-config/branch-sweep@v2.1
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

The action requires vergil-tooling on PATH (installed by a preceding shared/setup/vergil step) and a GH_TOKEN that can read the repo's pull requests and delete its branches.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description repo No ${{ github.repository }} Repository to sweep, as OWNER/NAME

docs.title: Token
docs.text: ops-github-config.yml mints a GitHub App token for this job with only contents: write (to delete the branch ref) and pull-requests: read (to decide which branches are finished). The token is scoped to the calling repo alone. The workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be used: a called workflow can only request the permissions the caller grants, and the standard ops.yml grants contents: read.

docs.title: Job summary
docs.text:
The summary lists each deleted branch with a link to its PR, in two groups:

  • Merged PR, branch not auto-deleted. The delete-on-merge setting should already have removed these. A leftover means GitHub skipped its after-merge processing, and the merge may also have fired no push event (the vergil-actions #951 case). This group is shown in a warning block, and each branch also gets a ::warning:: annotation on the run, so it stands out rather than being quietly cleaned up.
  • PR closed without merging. GitHub never deletes these on its own; the sweep is the expected cleanup when the delete-on-close rule missed one.

Errors are listed in a third group. The full vrg-branch-sweep output is included in a collapsed block.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
The step fails, and so does the job, when:

  • vrg-branch-sweep exits non-zero. A branch that could not be processed, a branch list that could not be read, and an authentication failure all count. The summary is still written first.
  • the per-branch lines cannot be reconciled with the sweep's own summary line (the deleted and error counts disagree, or the summary line is missing). This guards against a change in vrg-branch-sweep's output format silently producing an empty report.

The job does not use continue-on-error.

The reporting logic lives in sweep.sh so it is unit-testable; see actions/ops/github-config/branch-sweep/tests/sweep.test.sh, run by the smoke-branch-sweep.yml workflow.

docs.title: package/setup
docs.text:
Installs the package toolchain inside an arbitrary package build or install-test container: the OS prerequisites, a pinned uv, vergil-tooling, and (for build cells) a checksum-pinned nFPM. The containers are raw ubuntu or UBI images that ship neither Python nor vergil-tooling, and must run as root (the GitHub Actions container default).

This action is wired automatically into the build and install-test jobs of ci-package.yml and the package-build jobs of cd-release.yml. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v6
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/package/setup@v2.1
  with:
    nfpm: "true"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Description nfpm "false" Install nFPM. Build cells pass "true"; install-test cells leave it off.

docs.title: OS prerequisites
docs.text: The first step runs os-prereqs.sh, which keeps package jobs off slow apt mirrors and makes any apt stall fail fast instead of hanging the job.

docs.title: apt images (Ubuntu, Debian)
docs.text:
1. Mirror list on x86_64. The script rewrites the Ubuntu archive and security URIs, including any that already point at azure.archive.ubuntu.com, to mirror+file:/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt. It then writes that file in the format GitHub's hosted runner images use (configure-apt-sources.sh), one tab-separated entry per line:

    http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/    priority:1
http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/          priority:2
http://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/         priority:3

    apt tries the in-region Azure mirror first and moves down the list when a mirror fails. A failing Azure mirror therefore falls back instead of failing the job. On its own, a container image's default, archive.ubuntu.com, has stalled amd64 package builds for more than ten minutes.

    The hosts and priorities match runner-images, with one deliberate difference: the fallbacks use http://, not https://. A fresh container has no CA certificates until this script installs ca-certificates, so an https:// fallback fails with "No system certificates available". http:// is the image's own default, and apt still verifies every index against the archive's signed InRelease.

    The script rewrites both the deb822 /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources (24.04 and later) and the legacy /etc/apt/sources.list, before the first apt-get update. It writes the mirror list only when it rewrites a sources file, and overwrites the list rather than appending to it, so a re-run is a no-op. 2. arm64 is left alone. arm64 images use ports.ubuntu.com, which none of the listed mirrors serve, and which is already fast. Sources on any architecture other than x86_64 are not touched. 3. Fail-fast apt. The script writes /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-vergil-fast-fail:

    Acquire::Retries "3";
Acquire::Retries::Delay "false";
Acquire::http::Timeout "20";
Acquire::https::Timeout "20";
DPkg::Lock::Timeout "60";

    Every later apt call in the job inherits it, including the ones vergil-tooling makes during build and install-test.

    Acquire::Retries::Delay "false" is required for the mirror list to work. With apt's default delayed retries, apt 2.4 to 2.8 (Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04) deadlocks after a mirror-list failover: it fetches the fallback's InRelease files and then waits forever, and the timeouts never fire (LP #2003851). This is what hung vergil-tooling CD run 37678748594 for 21,578 seconds in package-sign, on a runner whose own sources are this mirror list. The same hang reproduces in an ubuntu:24.04 container with the Azure mirror unreachable. With undelayed retries, the same failover completes in seconds. 4. One update, one install. The script runs exactly one apt-get update. It then installs every prerequisite the package tooling needs in a single call: ca-certificates curl git tar gzip gnupg. Because they are all present, vergil-tooling's own bootstrap does not need to install them again.

docs.title: dnf images (UBI)
docs.text:
One dnf install with --setopt=retries=3 --setopt=timeout=20 installs ca-certificates /usr/bin/curl /usr/bin/gpg git tar gzip. curl and gpg are named by path, as vergil-tooling names them. UBI ships curl-minimal, which conflicts with the full curl package, and a path resolves to whichever package provides the file.

An image with neither apt-get nor dnf fails the step.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: The logic lives in os-prereqs.sh rather than inline YAML so that it can be tested. actions/package/setup/tests/os-prereqs.test.sh runs it against fixture /etc trees with recording apt-get/dnf stubs, so it needs neither root nor a container. It covers the deb822 x86_64 rewrite and the exact mirror-list contents, migrating Azure-pinned sources to the list, arm64 left untouched, the legacy sources.list, idempotence across two runs, an x86_64 image with no Ubuntu sources, the dnf path, and package-manager detection. The Smoke - setup/vergil outputs workflow runs it on every PR that touches this action.

docs.title: Job timeouts and the runner host
docs.text: package-sign in cd-release.yml installs rpm and gnupg on the runner host itself, not in a container. It passes the same fail-fast options on the command line (-o Acquire::Retries=3 -o Acquire::Retries::Delay=false -o Acquire::http::Timeout=20 -o Acquire::https::Timeout=20 -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60).
