docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• fix version-bump regex and correct VERSION to 1.1.2 (#136) The capture group in version-regex was preserving the major.minor. prefix, then {version} inserted the full next version, producing 1.1.1.1.2 instead of 1.1.2. Removed the capture group so the entire match is replaced with the next version.

  • create placeholder releases/index.md when no releases exist (#148) Pre-release repositories have releases/index.md in their mkdocs nav but no release note files yet. With strict mode enabled, mkdocs aborts on the missing file. Generate a placeholder index when no releases/*.md files are found.

  • install Trivy binary directly to avoid setup-trivy cache fallback failure (#152) The aquasecurity/trivy-action setup-trivy mechanism has a broken cache miss fallback that attempts to clone the trivy repo from source, which fails with 'couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/main'. This replaces setup-trivy with a direct binary download from GitHub releases and passes skip-setup-trivy: true to trivy-action, giving us full control over the Trivy version.

  • use setup-trivy with cache disabled instead of manual binary download (#153) The previous fix attempted a manual curl download with an incorrect version/URL. This uses the official setup-trivy action with cache disabled to avoid the broken cache miss fallback, then passes skip-setup-trivy to trivy-action.

  • replace aquasecurity GitHub actions with Docker-based Trivy execution (#154) The aquasecurity/trivy GitHub repo is empty (HTTP 409: 'Git Repository is empty'), causing both setup-trivy and trivy-action to fail when attempting to clone it. This replaces all aquasecurity GitHub actions with direct docker run commands using the aquasec/trivy Docker Hub image, which is still available and up to date (v0.69.1). A new trivy-image input allows pinning the version.

docs.text:
• drop auto-merge from version-bump-pr composite (bump 1.2.0) (#193) Step 2 of 3 for the poll-and-merge rework (plugin#57).

The composite used to end with:

gh pr merge --auto --merge --delete-branch <branch>

That call has been silently failing on every publish run since auto-merge was disabled fleet-wide — the bump PR got created, the step threw, the workflow was marked failure, and the user merged manually anyway.

Drop it. pr-url is already an output; the release skill drives the merge via st-merge-when-green once CI is green.

Action name / description, in-file comment, and public docs all updated to match. No other auto-merge references in the repo.

VERSION 1.1.4 -> 1.2.0. Minor bump because behavior changes for consumers pinned to @v1.1; the rolling tag will not move. They opt in to @v1.2 alongside a coordinated skill rewrite.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• use env vars + quoted heredoc in version-bump-pr Update step Surfaced on wphillipmoore/standard-tooling-plugin#78 (v1.4.1 publish): version-regex (\s*"version":\s*").*("\s*) contains literal double-quotes; GitHub expression interpolation put the raw value into the bash python3 -c "..." string, bash's outer double-quote closed at the first embedded ", the ( in the regex became a subshell-open, and the ) produced "unexpected token" at exit.

Latent since the step was written. Only surfaced once earlier composite failures (CHANGELOG merge, missing version-replacement) stopped masking it.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Pass values via env: and use a single-quoted heredoc delimiter <<'PYEOF' so bash performs zero interpolation on the body. The regex, replacement, and next version are all read from os.environ inside the python block.

No caller-visible change to the composite's interface (same inputs, same behavior). Patch-level bump — v1.2.0 consumers automatically get the fix when v1.2 rolls forward.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • map go to p/golang and capture scan exit codes The Semgrep registry uses p/golang, not p/go (HTTP 404). Added a language-name mapping so callers passing language: go get the correct ruleset. Also capture semgrep scan exit codes instead of letting bash -e kill the step, so the SARIF analysis step can provide diagnostics when the scan fails.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• handle missing primary-language in vergil.toml Use .get() with empty-string fallback instead of hard subscript when reading primary-language from vergil.toml. The key was removed in PR #609 but the docs deploy action still read it with a bare subscript, causing a KeyError in downstream CD pipelines. Ref #617

  • revert internal refs to @develop and replace trivy shell with vrg-trivy-scan All internal action references in reusable workflows were incorrectly frozen to @v2.0 on the develop branch. This broke self-referencing CI: changes merged to develop were never tested because workflows referenced old tagged code instead of the current branch. Reverted all 18 @v2.0 refs back to @develop so vrg-freeze-refs can properly rewrite them to exact patch versions at release time. Also replaced 80 lines of nested-shell-in-Docker trivy scan orchestration with vrg-trivy-scan, added Install vergil-tooling steps to codeql/trivy/semgrep jobs that were missing them. Ref #607, Ref #613

  • use local action paths for true self-referencing CI Replace all @develop action refs in reusable workflows with ./actions/ local paths. GitHub resolves ./ relative to the workflow file at the ref it was loaded from, so: during PR CI the actions come from the PR branch (true self-referencing), and at release time vrg-freeze-refs rewrites them to absolute tagged refs for downstream consumers. Ref #607, Ref #613

  • run trivy job in prod-base container Run the trivy CI job in the standard prod-base container instead of bare ubuntu-latest. This provides uv and other tooling needed by the Install vergil-tooling step. Ref #607

  • revert trivy action to original inline Docker approach Revert the trivy action to its original inline Docker implementation. The vrg-trivy-scan tool incorrectly wraps trivy in docker run rather than calling it directly, which needs to be fixed in vergil-tooling before the action can use it. See vergil-tooling#1246. Ref #607

  • use dev container prefix for CI Switch CI to use dev-base container images so we can test with updated container images before they are promoted to prod. Ref #607

  • eliminate shell injection patterns in action YAML files Move all expression interpolations out of run: script bodies and into env: blocks, referencing them as shell variables instead. This prevents expression injection where crafted input values could execute arbitrary commands during template expansion. Also fixes a bug in docs/deploy where the mike-command resolution step was referencing its own output instead of the input.

  • replace Docker orchestration with vrg-trivy-scan direct invocation Replace docker run wrapping in the trivy action with calls to vrg-trivy-scan for fs/image scans and direct trivy CLI for SBOM generation. The trivy job now runs in the container where trivy and vergil-tooling are available. Removes trivy-image and scanners inputs (no longer needed). Also converts the registry-publish trivy reference from @develop to local path.

docs.title: Chores
docs.text:
• remove invalid primary-language from vergil.toml Shell is no longer a valid value for primary-language, which is now only specified for the five main programming languages.

  • remove deprecated version-bump-pr action Remove the version-bump-pr composite action and all references to it. This action was deprecated in favor of the vrg-release orchestrator and is no longer referenced by any workflow. Removes the action directory, its docs page, and updates CLAUDE.md, mkdocs nav, action index, and configuration docs. Ref #603

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
• replace inline shell with vrg-semgrep-scan Replace 70 lines of embedded shell (ruleset resolution, scan execution, jq-based SARIF evaluation) with a single call to vrg-semgrep-scan from vergil-tooling. The tool handles language-to-ruleset mapping, scan execution with structured exit codes, SARIF parsing, finding evaluation, and GitHub Actions job summaries. The action retains Dockerfile/workflow auto-detection as lightweight shell checks that set --has-dockerfiles and --has-workflows flags. Ref #597

  • replace inline SARIF evaluation with vrg-sarif-evaluate Replace 27 lines of jq-based SARIF evaluation shell (nullglob, slurp, filtering, gating) with a single call to vrg-sarif-evaluate from vergil-tooling. The tool handles directory-mode SARIF parsing, severity filtering, structured annotations, and job summaries. Ref #598

  • replace inlined Python scripts with vrg-docs-stage and vrg-docs-patch-nav Replace two inlined Python heredoc scripts (release notes staging with semver-sorted index generation, and mkdocs.yml nav patching) with calls to vrg-docs-stage and vrg-docs-patch-nav from vergil-tooling. Eliminates the container path workaround from issue #204. Ref #599

  • replace case-statement command derivation with vrg-ecosystem-resolve Replace three duplicated case blocks (build command, publish command, credential secret) with a single call to vrg-ecosystem-resolve from vergil-tooling. The tool writes shell-compatible strings directly to GITHUB_OUTPUT with the correct key names. User overrides append after the tool call (last write wins). Ref #600

  • replace inline validation with vrg-release-validate-inputs Replace interdependent conditionals, loop-based language validation, and duplicated supported-languages list with a single call to vrg-release-validate-inputs from vergil-tooling. The tool shares the canonical language list with vrg-ecosystem-resolve. Ref #601

  • replace inline sed/grep logic with vrg-freeze-refs Replace two shell steps (sed-based regex freezing with temp file cleanup, and duplicated find/grep validation) with a single vrg-freeze-refs call from vergil-tooling. The tool handles YAML file collection, reference freezing, and unfrozen-ref validation in one pass. Ref #602

  • remove redundant auto-close check already handled by vrg-pr-issue-linkage The vrg-pr-issue-linkage tool already validates both issue linkage and auto-close keyword rejection. The inline shell step duplicated the auto-close check with jq extraction and grep regex. Ref #604

  • replace inline comparison with vrg-version-divergence Replace 22 lines of version comparison shell (conditional extraction, string comparison, multi-path output writes) with a single call to vrg-version-divergence from vergil-tooling. The tool handles version comparison logic, error messages, and job summaries. The action retains version extraction via user-provided commands and maps the exit code to the diverged boolean output. Ref #605

  • replace sed TOML parsing with python3 tomllib Replace the fragile sed regex that extracts the vergil version from vergil.toml with a python3 one-liner using the stdlib tomllib module. The sed approach could not handle comments, multi-line values, or quoted strings correctly. The vrg-resolve-tooling-version tool exists in vergil-tooling but cannot be used here due to a bootstrapping constraint: this action is what installs vergil-tooling, so the tool is not yet available when the action runs. Ref #606

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • resolve v2.0.21 breaking changes in release and trivy workflows Move vergil-tooling install before input validation in cd-release.yml, and make the trivy composite action self-contained by installing vergil-tooling when not already on PATH. Ref #631

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • run codeql job in container image The codeql job was the only security job running on a bare runner, causing uv: command not found failures because uv is only available in our container images. Ref #636

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• install uv via setup-uv when not present on bare runners The vergil-tooling setup action assumed uv was pre-installed, which breaks on bare ubuntu-latest runners used by CD pipelines. Add a conditional astral-sh/setup-uv step that only runs when uv is not found on PATH.

Replace duplicated vergil-tooling install logic in the Trivy action with delegation to the setup action, establishing a single source of truth for the install path.

  • use astral-sh/setup-uv@v7 (v8 has no rolling major tag)
  • use pip to install uv on bare runners instead of astral-sh/setup-uv Replace astral-sh/setup-uv with pip install to avoid a circular dependency: the repo allowlist compliance check rejects astral-sh/* until vergil-tooling is updated, but vergil-tooling can't be fixed until this action works on bare runners.

The pip approach matches how the Docker base images install uv and has no external action dependency. A follow-up issue (#643) tracks upgrading to astral-sh/setup-uv once the allowlist and compliance tooling are updated.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• revert to Docker-based approach for bare-runner compatibility The vrg-trivy-scan rewrite (commits 3e3f333b through c4956a80) broke CD pipelines on bare ubuntu-latest runners where the trivy binary is not installed. Restore the Docker-based approach that brings its own Trivy via aquasec/trivy:0.70.0, with injection-safe env: blocks (from 7290af2d).

Also remove the container directive from the ci-security trivy job since Docker-based Trivy runs on the host and does not need a container image.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • separate language and container-suffix inputs in cd-release.yml Add dedicated container-suffix input so non-language projects no longer misuse language: base. The container image line falls back through container-suffix, language, then 'base'. The validate-inputs action now treats language as optional and only passes it to the CLI when non-empty. Ref #653

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• run codeql on bare runner so autobuild has a language toolchain Commit 4d942b5b moved the codeql job into the prod-base container to silence 'uv: command not found' (ref #636), but prod-base ships no language toolchain. CodeQL autobuild for compiled languages (go, java, rust) needs the compiler on PATH, so it failed fleet-wide with 'go: executable file not found in $PATH' on every consuming repo pinned to @v2.0.

Language images are published per-version only (prod-go:1.25, prod-go:1.26) with no prod-:latest tag, and a job-level container directive cannot resolve a concrete version inline, so the language-container route is a dead end. The uv concern that motivated the container was independently handled ~45 min later in setup/vergil (84bf315e, fd62605c), which now installs uv on bare runners.

Dropping the container restores the pre-regression bare-runner execution that passed CodeQL on 2026-05-27. The runner supplies every language toolchain autobuild needs; setup/vergil supplies uv for vrg-sarif-evaluate.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
• add build-only docs verification to PR CI Add a reusable ci-docs.yml workflow that stages the docs the same way the CD docs deploy does and runs mkdocs build --strict — build only, no mike, no push, no credentials. Documentation that fails to build is now caught pre-merge as a CI gate instead of post-merge in the CD docs job.

Factor the changelog/release-notes staging and nav patching into a shared actions/shared/docs/stage composite action used by both ci-docs and cd/docs/deploy, so CI and CD build the docs identically and a green CI docs check predicts a green CD deploy. The deploy action no longer stages inline; cd-docs.yml runs the shared stage step before deploy.

The CI workflow self-guards on mkdocs config presence so repos without docs are unaffected, and is wired into this repo's own ci.yml on the default prod container for parity with the cd-docs deploy.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • treat missing origin/main as a first-release no-op A repo with no origin/main is in a legitimate bootstrap / pre-release state: nothing ships without main, so there is no published version to diverge from. The fetch step previously ran 'git fetch origin main' unconditionally, which exits 128 (couldn't find remote ref main) and failed the whole version-bump job, permanently blocking PRs on repos whose only long-lived branch is develop. The gate now probes the remote with 'git ls-remote --exit-code': a genuinely absent main is treated as a first-release no-op (job goes green), while real fetch/network errors (any other non-zero exit) remain fatal so they are not masked. The compare step already tolerated an empty main version. Closes the hard-failure described in issue #672.

• add v2.0→v2.1 canary design (#679) Design for piloting the fleet-wide vergil 2.0→2.1 migration in vergil-actions as the lowest-risk, self-referential canary. Records the pin-driven cache mechanism, the two-line functional change, verification flow, risk surface, and the lockstep generalization that feeds the fleet playbook (vergil-tooling#1371).

  • revise v2.0→v2.1 canary design after pushback (#679) Pushback review surfaced four corrections: the version-divergence gate requires a VERSION bump (pin-only PR fails CI); a stale absolute action ref (standards-compliance setup/vergil@v2.0) must become @develop; acceptance splits into a CI gate and a CD gate because the PR never runs the release path where the 2.1 deltas live; and the doc scope includes the README @v2.0 consumer examples. Adds the two-version-axes explanation and folds the new lessons into the fleet generalization.

  • drop unneeded VERSION bump from canary design (#679) Verified origin/main=2.1.0 and develop=2.1.1, so a feature branch off develop already diverges from main and the version-divergence gate passes without a VERSION bump. Removes the erroneously-added VERSION change, returning the set to three changes (pin, standards-compliance ref, docs), and records the divergence-state check as the general rule.

  • expand canary doc scope to full @v2.0 sweep (#679) Discovered ~66 stale @v2.0 consumer references (11 in the workflows README, 55 across the published docs site) beyond the originally-scoped handful. Per decision, the canary does a full sweep of current consumer-facing refs to @v2.1, excluding historical records under docs/specs and docs/plans.

  • add v2.0→v2.1 canary implementation plan (#679) Task-by-task plan for the three-change set (tooling pin, standards-compliance @develop ref, full consumer-doc @v2.0 sweep), local validation gate, and PR/CI gate, with the CD gate and playbook implementation as follow-ups.

  • note no-auto-close-keyword PR constraint (#679) The standards-compliance check (vrg-pr-issue-linkage) rejects Closes/Fixes keywords, so migration PRs must link the issue without them. Captured in the CI-gate section and flagged as a per-repo playbook item; surfaced during alignment review of the implementation plan.

  • bump consumer @v2.0 references to v2.1 (#679) Sweep all current consumer-facing version refs onto the v2.1 line: CLAUDE.md host-install (v1.4 to v2.1), 11 refs in the workflows README, and 55 across the published docs site. docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • fully-qualify the nested cd-docs reusable ref (#751) (#752) cd-docs-refresh is a reusable workflow called cross-repo, but it nested cd-docs.yml via a relative './.github/workflows/cd-docs.yml' — which does not resolve when the outer workflow is invoked from another repo via a tag (GitHub reports 'workflow was not found'), and which vrg-freeze-refs never pins. Make it a fully-qualified '@develop' ref so it resolves cross-repo and the release freeze rewrites it to the release tag. Fixes the org docs repos' daily cd-docs-refresh startup failure.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• key first-release no-op off release tags, not missing main (#758) The version-divergence gate's first-release escape hatch guarded the wrong condition: it keyed off a missing origin/main. But the bootstrap wizard creates and pushes main at init, so main always exists on a brand-new repo, making the hatch unreachable. Every release-bearing repo's first PR into develop then hard-failed the gate with 'version not bumped: head (0.1.0) == main (0.1.0)' — there was no way to satisfy it, since nothing had been released.

Detect the first release from the real signal instead: the absence of a release tag. tag-and-release stamps every release with a vX.Y.Z tag, so no such tag means no release has occurred. This distinguishes the two EQUAL cases exactly — bootstrap (no tag) passes; a genuine missed bump after a prior release (tag exists) still fails — regardless of whether main exists. The fetch and compare steps now run only once a release exists.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• codify the all-hard-gates principle (#765)
  • docs(ci): codify the all-hard-gates principle

Add a foundational-principles doc to the CI Gate Requirements section stating that every check that matters is a hard, asserting gate — there are no report-only or warning gates, because an unheeded warning is meaningless (reviewers optimize for can-I-merge and never revisit warnings). Deprecation warnings are treated as errors (early signal of a future outage), and the sprawling warning-exception list is rejected: if it matters, assert it and fail on it.

Cross-references the CI-evidence publish-safety property (epic vergil-project/.github#140 spec §9.1), which depends on this principle. Wired into the mkdocs nav and the ci-gates section index.

Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#763

  • docs(ci): distinguish gate deployment lifecycle from soft gates

Add a gate-deployment-lifecycle section to the all-hard-gates doc reconciling the all-hard-gates principle with staged rollout. All gates are hard as a permanent configuration — a permanent soft gate does not exist — but deploying a new hard gate is a lifecycle: it first runs in warning mode (reports, does not fail) for a bounded bake-in period to collect reliability data, then is promoted to enforcing (fatal) once proven stable.

Warning mode is a transient deployment state of a hard gate, never a permanent soft gate; the end state of every gate is always enforcing. Uses the CI-evidence gate (epic vergil-project/.github#140) as the concrete example: warning mode first, bake across release cadence, single flag flip to enforcing. This refines rather than contradicts the existing content — the unheeded-warning anti-pattern is the permanent report-only case, not the time-boxed, owned, promotion-committed deployment stage.

Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#763

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• emit ci-evidence- artifacts from gate workflows (#764) Add a shared actions/ci/evidence/emit composite that writes an evidence.json fragment ({gate, tools, metrics, files}) and uploads it, together with any available report files, as a ci-evidence- workflow-run artifact for the release-time harvester (vrg-ci-evidence).

    Wire it into all four required gate workflows via a dedicated needs-gated evidence job so the artifact's presence is itself proof the gate passed, and so each gate emits exactly one artifact despite its matrix/multi-job structure (upload-artifact forbids same-name uploads across jobs):

    • ci-test, ci-audit, ci-quality: one evidence job that runs after the gate's check jobs succeed.
    • ci-security: each scanner (codeql, trivy, semgrep) uploads its SARIF as an evidence partial UNCONDITIONALLY (independent of the code-scanning upload), and a consolidation job merges the partials into the single ci-evidence-security artifact. This lets the harvester read artifacts only, with no code-scanning API dependency (spec section 7).

    Report-file globs (coverage.xml, junit.xml, pip-audit.json, licenses.json) are forward-compatible: they are skipped until the check commands emit them, so test/audit/quality currently produce an evidence.json-only artifact, which is sufficient for completeness.

    Task T8 of epic vergil-project/.github#140.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • pass GH_TOKEN to the docs stage step so evidence links resolve (#772) The 'Stage changelog and release notes' step runs vrg-docs-stage, which links each release page to its CI-evidence bundle via 'gh release view'. Its env block set only MKDOCS_CONFIG, so gh was unauthenticated and the docs job failed. Wire GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} into the same env block; both docs workflows already grant the required contents permission. The nav-patch step (vrg-docs-patch-nav) makes no gh calls and is unchanged. Ref #770

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• harvest, attest, and attach CI evidence (warning mode) (#771) Add the actions/cd/release/ci-evidence composite and wire it as the first publish step of cd-release.yml (evidence-first, spec §9). Ships in WARNING mode (spec §9.2): non-fatal and timeout-bounded so it can never abort a release; promotion to enforcing (Task T11) is a single flip of the evidence-enforce default.

The composite runs vrg-ci-evidence bundle (bounded by the coreutils timeout command, since composite steps cannot use timeout-minutes), attests the bundle digest via actions/attest-build-provenance, and attaches the tarball plus manifest with gh release upload --clobber. Bundle and upload are bash steps that capture the exit code under set +e and, in warning mode, convert any failure or timeout into a ::warning:: and exit 0. The attest step is a uses step that a composite cannot wrap, so the call-site continue-on-error tracks evidence-enforce, keeping warning mode non-aborting even on a rare attest failure.

Add actions: read to the cd-release job permissions so the harvest can list and download the release PR's ci-evidence-* artifacts (spec §5.2); the consuming repo's cd.yml must grant the same scope.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• split cd-release evidence into pre-publish gate + post-release attach (#777) T9 (#769) ran the whole CI-evidence step first, but two things it needs are created later in the same job: the GitHub Release (gh release upload's target, created by tag-and-release) and the SBOM (built by registry-publish). So in warning mode the upload warned and attached nothing, and the bundle omitted the SBOM. Split the single ci-evidence composite in two:

  • ci-evidence-gate (stays first, pre-publish): resolve the release PR, harvest the required gate evidence, and validate completeness. Once enforcing, incomplete evidence fails here before anything is published (spec §9).

  • ci-evidence-attach (new, after tag-and-release): assemble the complete bundle now including the built SBOM, attest it, and upload it to the Release that now exists.

Both composites invoke the existing vrg-ci-evidence bundle CLI and keep the warning-mode contract: set +e captures the exit code so any failure/timeout becomes a ::warning:: and exits 0, and the call-site continue-on-error tracks evidence-enforce so even the uses: attest step cannot abort the release. Promotion to enforcing (T11) stays a pure flip of the evidence-enforce default, which flips both steps' fatality and both continue-on-error guards at once.

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
• share one harvest across evidence gate and attach (#782) Rewire the cd-release CI-evidence gate and attach composites to share a single artifact harvest instead of each running the atomic bundle (which re-downloaded the release PR's artifacts).

The gate now calls vrg-ci-evidence harvest (network download + validate_completeness gate), persisting the downloaded evidence and harvest-state.json into a shared staging dir on the job workspace (${{ github.workspace }}/.ci-evidence-staging). The attach now calls vrg-ci-evidence assemble --staging <same-dir>, which is fully network-free and produces the tarball + standalone manifest offline. Both composites run in the same cd-release job, so the workspace filesystem persists between them and the release's artifacts are downloaded exactly once.

Warning-mode wrappers and the enforce flag are preserved exactly in both steps; the attest and gh release upload steps are unchanged. Part 2 of the double-harvest fix (Part 1 is the vergil-tooling CLI split, #2330).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • explicit CD secrets and semgrep rule-exclusion docs (#788) Document vrg-semgrep-scan's repeatable --exclude-rule flag, the additive DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_RULES fleet baseline, and the temporary fleet-wide github-actions-mutable-action-tag exemption pending vergil-project/.github#194 (with our own @v2.1 refs as a permanent exception). Document that cd-release callers forward explicit least-privilege publishing secrets per ecosystem instead of blanket secrets: inherit; generated cd.yml emits an explicit secrets block or none accordingly.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• route C++ CI to compiler-family images with per-kind cardinality (#793) Extend the reusable ci-*.yml workflows to accept language: cpp and run the C++ pipeline per compiler-family image.

A new actions/ci/matrix composite action resolves the per-version job matrix from the flat versions input: for cpp it splits each clang-/gcc- token and routes it to prod-cpp-clang: / prod-cpp-gcc:, and it emits an 'all' matrix (per-version) plus a 'once' matrix collapsed to the primary version. ci-quality/ci-test/ci-audit gain a matrix prep job and consume all (typecheck, unit) or once (lint, dependencies) so the emitted job/gate names line up exactly with github_config.desired_ci_gates_ruleset for a cpp repo: per-version typecheck/test, run-once lint/audit keyed to the primary clang tag. Non-cpp languages resolve byte-identical images and keep per-version cardinality.

ci-security wires Semgrep p/c and p/cpp for cpp via extra-config (C++ has no single p/ ruleset); CodeQL already forwards the cpp language and cpp is CodeQL-supported. Adds a C++ example to the workflow README.

Ref vergil-project/.github#207

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• gate follows release-model instead of run-release wiring Make ci-version-bump.yml self-guard on the consuming repo's vergil.toml: when release-model is "none" the gate steps do not run and the job passes, so non-releasing repos no longer need to pass run-release: false (the skip escape hatch flagged in #674).

The run-release input is kept for backwards compatibility but is now deprecated: passing false still suppresses the gate and emits a ::warning:: annotation pointing at the calling workflow. Removal is tracked in #688.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• describe dynamic cached-image tooling install CLAUDE.md claimed vergil-tooling CLI tools and validators are pre-installed in the dev container images. The base images contain no vergil-tooling; it is installed dynamically. Rewrite the Environment Setup and Standard-Tooling Integration passages to describe the per-branch cached-image mechanism (vrg-container-run builds :---- with the version pinned in vergil.toml, cache keyed on lockfiles plus vergil.toml) and the CI-side dynamic install via the actions/shared/setup/vergil action. Also fix the stale actions/shared/setup/vergil-tooling path in the action list.

  • replace vrg-docker-run, fix v1.4 pin and pre-installed claim The docs-site and legacy development docs referenced the removed vrg-docker-run command (renamed vrg-container-run), told users to install vergil-tooling@v1.4 (the repo pins v2.1 in vergil.toml), and claimed the dev-base container has every required tool pre-installed. Static linters and docs tools are baked into the base image, but vrg-validate itself arrives via the per-branch cached image that vrg-container-run builds with the vergil.toml-pinned version.

    • Rename the command everywhere (including the CLI-reference link anchor in workflows/index.md), bump the install snippet to v2.1, and rewrite the validation and environment pages to distinguish baked-in tools from the dynamically installed vergil-tooling, matching the corrected CLAUDE.md description from #684.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• skip pip's vendored SBOM in fs/image vuln scans (#798)
  • fix(trivy): skip pip's vendored SBOM in fs/image vuln scans

pip 26.x ships pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json, a CycloneDX SBOM of pip's vendored dependencies. Trivy ingests it and reports those vendored packages (e.g. setuptools 70.3.0, msgpack 1.1.2) as findings even though they are pip internals, not the scan target's attack surface — breaking the docker-publish gate on every pip-bearing image fleet-wide.

Add --skip-files '**/pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json' to the fs and image vuln scans so Trivy no longer parses that SBOM. The sbom generation mode is left untouched (an SBOM should describe everything present).

Verified against the real vergil-containers prod-base image on Trivy 0.71.0 (the action default) and 0.72.0: the skip clears the setuptools and msgpack false positives while every other finding still reports. Lets consumer repos drop their per-image rm workaround (vergil-containers#481).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• wire CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER into ci-audit workflow (#803) Declare the ConanCenter provider token as an optional workflow_call secret in ci-audit.yml and inject it into the dependency-audit step's env: so conan audit can authenticate inside the container. Threaded via the explicit-secret chain (never secrets: inherit, per epics #189/#197).

The token is cpp-only; when the caller leaves it unset the cpp audit path skips the conan gate with a notice rather than failing auth. Documents the caller-side secret passing for cpp repos in the workflows README and ci-audit docs page.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• install declared [container].system-packages on CI test jobs (#808)
  • feat(ci): install declared system-packages on CI test jobs

Add actions/shared/setup/system-packages composite action: reads the declared [container].system-packages via vrg-container-system-packages --install-script and apt-installs them with bounded retry (mirror-flake tolerance) and fail-closed behaviour (a missing candidate exhausts retries and exits non-zero with the speller's package+platform message). The retry/fail-closed loop lives in install.sh so it is unit-testable; action.yml is a thin wrapper. Wired into the unit job of ci-test.yml after Install vergil-tooling — test-runtime only, not lint/typecheck (spec 3.3). Epic vergil-project/.github#272.

  • test(ci): cover system-packages install retry and fail-closed paths

Self-contained, framework-free harness (this repo declares language=shell, which runs no test gate and ships no action-test convention) for install.sh: PATH-stubs vrg-container-system-packages and apt-get to exercise the installable happy path, the fail-closed bogus-package path (non-zero exit with the 'not installable' message), the transient-flake retry-then-success path, and the no-packages skip. Epic vergil-project/.github#272.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• document CI system-packages setup step (#813) Add operator-facing docs for the shared/setup/system-packages composite action and its auto-wiring into the ci-test reusable workflow.

  • New Action Reference page (actions/shared-setup-system-packages.md) with behavior, single-speller apt install, bounded retry, fail-closed on a missing candidate, and test-runtime-only scope; added to the mkdocs nav and the actions index.

  • ci-test workflow reference: note the declared system-packages install on test jobs only (lint/typecheck excluded).
  • configuration.md: cross-reference pointer to the [container].system-packages key's CI effect.

Cross-links to the consuming-repo key docs in vergil-tooling (#2724) rather than restating them. Operator-side companion to vergil-tooling#2724.

Refs vergil-project/.github#272; action #808 (issue #807); issue #812

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• TypeScript support in reusable workflows (#815) Accept language: typescript in the reusable CI workflows.

  • Matrix routing: node- version tokens resolve to prod-ts-node: images (ts-node suffix + numeric tag), mirroring C++ token routing. Extracted the resolver to actions/ci/matrix/resolve.sh with a unit test.

  • Cardinality: TYPECHECK/LINT/AUDIT run once (collapsed to the primary Node version via the matrix once output); only TEST fans out per Node version. The typecheck job now consumes once for TypeScript, matching the run-once gates desired_ci_gates_ruleset keys to ci.versions[0].
  • CodeQL mapping: primary-language typescript maps to javascript-typescript and cpp maps to c-cpp via one table in actions/ci/security/codeql/resolve-language.sh (bare typescript is not a valid CodeQL analysis language). Unit-tested.
  • Semgrep: wire p/typescript for TypeScript repos.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add shared/setup/build-command CI step (fail-closed, no retry) (#820) Add a composite action that runs a repo's declared [container].build-command in CI, read through the vrg-container-build-command speller shipped in vergil-tooling v2.1.189.

Unlike the sibling system-packages action (bounded apt retry), the build command is fail-closed with NO retry: an arbitrary build command that fails is a real failure, not a transient mirror flake. Logic lives in install.sh with a self-contained behavioural harness (tests/install.test.sh) covering execute, fail-closed-no-retry, and skip-when-undeclared.

Wired into ci-test.yml's unit job after system-packages (test-runtime dependency only). Docs and mkdocs nav mirror the system-packages action.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• export NODE_PATH in the build-command step for CI resolution parity (#825) After the declared [container].build-command runs, export NODE_PATH (the npm global root from npm root -g) to $GITHUB_ENV so subsequent CI test steps can resolve a node library baked out-of-workspace by the build-command (npm install -g ) via CommonJS require. This mirrors the NODE_PATH the local dev image injects (vergil-project/vergil-tooling#2781), keeping baked-library resolution identical locally and in CI — the drift epic vergil-project/.github#291 prevents.

    The export is guarded on CI context ($GITHUB_ENV present) and npm being on PATH, so a non-CI or non-node run is a clean no-op; the step stays fail-closed and retry-free. NODE_PATH is honoured by require only (ESM import ignores it).

    Extends the install.test.sh harness with two cases (NODE_PATH appended when a command ran with a stub npm on PATH; nothing appended on the skip path) and documents the behavior and the require-only caveat.

Also add a back-link from the system-packages action page to its build-command sibling. docs.title: Features
docs.text: • promote CI evidence gate to enforcing (#832) Flip the evidence-enforce default from false to true in cd-release.yml (and the two composites' inert enforce defaults, for a self-consistent fail-closed default). Incomplete or failed CI evidence now hard-fails a release before publish — the spec §9 publish invariant. Warning mode remains as a temporary per-repo opt-out (evidence-enforce=false), never a permanent soft gate. Promotion follows a clean ~4-week bake: 54/54 vergil-tooling releases (v2.1.138-191) and 100% bundle attachment across the other cd-release repos within their adoption windows, with complete manifests. Completes T11 of epic vergil-project/.github#140.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • bridge per-matrix report files into test/audit/quality evidence artifacts (#837) In GitHub Actions each job runs on its own runner with its own filesystem. The test/audit/quality exec (matrix) jobs produced their report files, but the separate evidence job did a clean checkout and called evidence/emit against globs that matched an empty tree, stranding every report and shipping empty payloads for those three gates while only security carried real files. Mirror the working ci-security.yml pattern: each matrix leg uploads its version-suffixed reports as a per-version partial artifact, and the evidence job downloads every leg's partials (merge-multiple) before emit, so the bundle carries each interpreter version's reports. quality-ruff.json / quality-mypy.xml are a locked filename contract with vergil-tooling#2811 and stay skipped-empty (non-fatal) until it releases.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • provide GH_TOKEN to cd-docs pre-deploy step (#845) The pre-deploy step runs vrg-roadmap / vrg-activity-log, which shell out to gh to read the org .github epics. In an Actions runner gh exits non-zero without a token, so every CD docs-refresh job failed. The org .github epic home is public, so the repo-scoped default token is sufficient; set GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} on the step. No wrapper or caller changes needed. Ref vergil-project/.github#310.

Preserves the 2026-05-19 baseline (5.5/10) and adds a freshly re-run 2026-08-12 snapshot (5.5/10, commit bbaccdd4). Format and location mirror the vergil-claude-plugin capture. Remediation remains tracked separately (epic vergil-project/.github#54, tracking issue vergil-project/vergil-tooling#828).

  • update the all-hard-gates CI-evidence example to enforcing (#843) The CI-evidence completeness gate reached its enforcing end state after a ~4-week bake (evidence-enforce flipped false->true, live as of v2.1.27). The worked example in the all-hard-gates principle doc still described it in present-tense warning mode, which is stale. Rewrite the example as a lifecycle that ran to completion — introduced in warning mode, baked while robustness was validated, then promoted by a single flag flip to enforcing — and state the present end state plainly: an incomplete or failed evidence bundle is now a terminal, publish-blocking failure. Also document that completeness is now measured against report payload, not just envelope presence (ref #2812), and note the two current residuals (empty manifest metrics, empty security tools) as open limitations.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• wire a C++ semgrep ruleset that exists (#851) (#852) p/cpp is not a Semgrep registry ruleset - it 404s, so the semgrep gate failed with exit 7 on every cpp repo. p/c-plus-plus and p/cplusplus 404 as well.

p/c alone is not a fix. extra-config is the entire C++ ruleset here, because vrg-semgrep-scan's _LANGUAGE_RULESETS has no cpp key, and p/c applies rules to .c only - it scans no C++ whatsoever. Dropping to p/c would have turned a hard failure into silent zero coverage.

Measured with an identical probe.c/probe.cpp pair on semgrep 1.173.0, reading paths.scanned: p/c scans only the .c file, while p/security-audit, p/default and p/cwe-top-25 all apply rules to the .cpp file. p/security-audit also fired a real finding on the C probe (insecure-use-string-copy-fn, CWE-676). Full table in the issue.

Surfaced by logical-minds-foundry/mq-protocol-gateway, the fleet's first cpp repo.

  • state plainly that semgrep gives no C++ coverage (#853) (#854) Follow-up to #851/#852, which stopped the p/cpp 404 but documented p/security-audit as restoring C++ rule applicability. That claim is false and the config did not do it.

No community Semgrep pack declares a single cpp rule - measured p/c 0, p/security-audit 0, p/default 0, p/cwe-top-25 0. https://semgrep.dev/c/r/cpp returns 200 with a body of 'rules: []': the C++ namespace exists and is empty, which is also why p/cpp was never published.

The earlier conclusion came from reading semgrep's paths.scanned, where p/security-audit appeared to scan a .cpp probe. That was its 14 generic/regex rules matching any file, not C++ analysis. Direct check with gets(buf) duplicated across t.c/t.cpp/t.cc/t.hpp under --config p/c: 'Scanning 4 files tracked by git with 2 Code rules: Scanning 1 file with 2 c rules', one finding, on t.c only.

Semgrep's GA C/C++ support is Semgrep Code - Pro engine and Pro rules behind SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN - not the unauthenticated community registry this pipeline scans.

docs.title: Breaking change — ci-security.yml callers must grant actions: read
docs.text:
This release adds actions: read to the permissions: request of the reusable ci-security.yml workflow. GitHub validates that request against the calling job's permissions at workflow startup, so every caller must add actions: read to the permissions: block of the job that calls ci-security.yml before consuming this release. Callers without the grant fail at startup, with no checks registered:

The workflow is requesting 'actions: read', but is only allowed 'actions: none'.

The grant is backward-compatible with v2.1.2 (callers may grant more than a called workflow requests), so consumers can land it before upgrading. The v2.1 rolling tag was rolled back to v2.1.2 when this release first broke consumers, and is re-promoted once all consumers carry the grant. Full incident analysis and rollout plan: #698.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• grant actions: read and add upload-sarif artifact fallback (#694) SARIF upload to code scanning fails on private consumer repos because codeql-action/upload-sarif reads the workflow run via the Actions API, which needs actions: read there; public repos do not, so the gap was invisible on vergil-project repos.

  • Add actions: read at the workflow level and to the codeql, trivy, and semgrep job permissions in ci-security.yml, and to this repo's own caller in ci.yml.

  • Add an upload-sarif input (default true) to ci-security.yml and to the trivy and semgrep actions. When false, scans still run and still fail on findings, but SARIF results are attached as build artifacts (trivy-fs-sarif, semgrep-sarif) instead of being uploaded to code scanning — the documented posture for private repos without GHAS.
  • Gate the codeql job on upload-sarif: CodeQL cannot run on private repos without GHAS regardless of upload destination.
  • Document the permission and the no-GHAS configuration across the workflow, action, and CI-gates docs.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• use python3 from PATH, not /usr/local/bin (#863) (#864) The 'Detect release model' step invoked /usr/local/bin/python3. That path exists in the base/python images - where this workflow's own ci.yml self-test runs (container-suffix: base) - but NOT in prod-cpp-clang:20, where python3 is at /usr/bin/python3. So the version-bump job hard-failed for any cpp repo with 'No such file or directory', before evaluating any version.

Confirmed in the cpp image: /usr/local/bin/python3 is absent; python3 from PATH is /usr/bin/python3 (3.13.5, tomllib present) and reads release-model correctly. Using python3 from PATH resolves to the right interpreter in every image and makes the step image-agnostic - the workflow should not assume a python location.

Surfaced by logical-minds-foundry/mq-protocol-gateway#1 (first cpp repo): PR #12 was green on every job except version/version-bump, purely because of this path.

docs.text:
• stop declaring signing secrets that shadow the package-signing environment (#913) (#914) The first packaged release (vergil-project/packages v1.1.0, CD run 37494464077) failed closed: package-sign saw an empty PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY, although the package-signing environment was applied (deployment on main 16:17:57Z) and holds the secret. cd-release declared PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY/PASSPHRASE under on.workflow_call.secrets (to satisfy actionlint), and a declared-but-unpassed secret shadowed the environment secret with an empty value.

Remove both declarations so the environment is the only source (matching publish-index, which declares none), and ignore actionlint's resulting undeclared-secret finding for exactly those two names in .github/actionlint.yaml. Document the rule.

docs.text: • upload SARIF without accepted-suppressed results (#921) Code scanning ignores SARIF suppressions, so a finding the SARIF gate accepts (e.g. a justified nosemgrep) still failed GitHub's Semgrep OSS check. The Semgrep and Trivy actions now run vrg-sarif-filter and upload a filtered *.upload.sarif copy, while the unfiltered SARIF remains what the evidence job collects. The ci-security trivy job installs vergil-tooling to provide the filter. CodeQL is unchanged: analyze uploads internally. Docs updated. Requires a vergil-tooling release containing vrg-sarif-filter (vergil-project/vergil-tooling#3114). Ref #920

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • callers must pass secrets: inherit for environment secrets (#918) (#919) A controlled probe (vergil-project/packages#6, run 37507168545) proved that environment secrets reach a job in a cross-repo reusable workflow only when the caller passes secrets: inherit; an explicit map or nothing gives an empty value, and the callee's declaration is irrelevant. Correct the cd-release and publish-index caller docs and examples (inherit plus a scoped nosemgrep), and correct the #913 comments, which attributed the failure to secret shadowing (disproven).

docs.text:
• Azure-first apt mirror list, fail-fast apt and job timeouts for package jobs (#933)
  • fix(package): use the Azure apt mirror and fail-fast apt in package setup

Move the package setup OS-prerequisites step into os-prereqs.sh. On x86_64 Ubuntu containers it points the archive and security URIs (deb822 ubuntu.sources and legacy sources.list) at http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/, the mirror GitHub's hosted runners use, before the single apt-get update; arm64 (ports.ubuntu.com) is left untouched. It writes /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-vergil-fast-fail (3 retries, 20 s timeouts) for every later apt call in the job, installs all prerequisites including gnupg in one call, and on UBI runs one dnf install with retries=3/timeout=20 and path-form curl/gpg. derive.sh now runs vrg-ci-resolve once and copies its answer to the setup action's outputs, adding container-tags and container-suffixes; the inline Python derivation is gone and resolver errors fail the step as ::error:: annotations. ci/matrix builds every image from the resolver's tags and suffixes with no family routing, and run-once kinds follow the primary version. • pin Python legs to the image's interpreter with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system (#995)
  • ci(toolchain): pin Python legs to the image's interpreter with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system

Every Python matrix leg (ci-quality lint and typecheck, ci-audit dependencies, ci-test unit) now pins uv through a new ci/toolchain/pin-python action, which exports UV_PYTHON= and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system. A repo's uv python-preference (e.g. only-managed) can no longer make a leg download a managed Python instead of using the image's; a missing interpreter fails loudly. The pin.test.sh harness also checks that every job with an assert-toolchain step pins through the action and that no workflow sets UV_PYTHON by hand. assert-toolchain now logs the interpreter path it found. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#994

An in-place edit dropped the mode to 644 in the previous commit. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#994

• pull from GHCR mirror with retry; bump to 0.71.0 (#706) The shared Trivy action pulled aquasec/trivy from Docker Hub anonymously with no retry, so transient Hub timeouts and anonymous rate limits turned the security/trivy check red on unrelated diffs (e.g. vergil-claude-plugin PR #475).

  • Default the image to the GHCR mirror ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy, which sidesteps Docker Hub's anonymous pull rate limits entirely. GHCR is the natural registry from GitHub Actions runners and needs no Hub-token secret plumbed through consuming repos.

  • Bump the default tag to 0.71.0 (released 2026-06-01) for freshness.
  • Add a bounded pull-with-backoff step before the scan steps as a registry-agnostic backstop; subsequent docker run steps reuse the local image.

docs.text:
• pin the docs jobs' uv interpreter source with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system (#1005)
  • ci(docs): pin the docs jobs' uv interpreter source with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system

The ci-docs and cd-docs jobs ran uv run mkdocs/mike for Python repos without UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE, so a repo with python-preference = only-managed made uv download a managed Python for the docs build, or fail when it also set python-downloads = manual. Both jobs now set UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system in their job env (source only; they resolve no version, so UV_PYTHON stays unset). The cd/docs/deploy action pins its Deploy docs step for direct callers, and setup/vergil pins the vergil-tooling self-install uv sync inline. The pin.test.sh harness gains a uv source guard: every workflow job running a uv project command or ci/toolchain/assert must pin first (pin-python or job env), and every composite action or script must pin on the step or inline, with assert (caller-pinned) and package/setup/detect.sh (needs managed Python) as listed exceptions; fixtures test the guard both ways. smoke-setup-vergil now triggers on any workflow or action change. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#1002

  • ci(toolchain): restore the executable bit on pin.test.sh

An in-place sed edit dropped the mode to 644 in the previous commit. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#1002

docs.text: • make detect.sh ignore the repo's uv settings with uv run --no-config (#1010) detect.sh read vergil.toml with uv run --no-project --python 3.14, which still reads the repo's uv settings ([tool.uv] in pyproject.toml, uv.toml) from the working directory. In a repo that sets python-downloads = "manual" (with python-preference = "only-managed") it failed in the package images, which ship no Python and need uv to download one. It now runs uv run --no-config --no-project, so the repo's uv settings cannot reach it. detect.test.sh gains cases that run detect.sh from inside a fixture repo with those settings in pyproject.toml and in uv.toml, with an empty managed-Python dir, and assert the same install spec. The pin.test.sh source guard no longer exempts detect.sh outright: it is now a config-free file whose every uv command must pass --no-config, with fixtures both ways. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#1003

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• test the warning passthrough with a stub resolver; app multi-pin is fatal (#1023) The released resolver (vergil-tooling 2.1.259+) makes an app pinning more than one version a fatal error (T14, vergil-tooling#3372) and prints no warnings (vergil-tooling#3442), so the derive.sh harness case that expected a ::warning:: for that pin failed on every PR. Replace it with a case that drives derive.sh's warning passthrough through a stub vrg-ci-resolve (same five-key JSON shape), add a case asserting the app multi-pin fails with the resolver's ::error::, and update the derive.sh comment and action docs. Ref #1022.

  • derive the release container tag from the resolver (#1024) The release job ran on the caller's container-tag input, which vrg-repo-init freezes into cd.yml at init time, so releases built on a stale version outside the window. A new setup job runs the shared setup action (vrg-ci-resolve) and the release job's image, and its validate-inputs check, now use its primary-container-tag, as CI's single-container jobs do. The container-tag input stays for one release as accepted-but-ignored with a ::warning::, because GitHub rejects an undeclared input to a reusable workflow and every caller still passes it; vergil-project/vergil-tooling#3484 removes it from the callers. Adds the container-tag.test.sh harness and smoke-cd-release workflow, and a cd-release workflow docs page. Ref #1017

docs.text: <ul> <li>derive the release image suffix from the resolver (#1030) The release job built its image suffix from the caller's container-suffix, else language, else base, so a C++ caller passing language: cpp got the unpublished prod-cpp image. The setup job now runs the new cd/release/primary-suffix action on the shared setup action's primary-version and container-suffixes, and the release job runs on prod-:, the image CI's primary leg uses (clang-20 -> prod-cpp-clang:20). The caller's container-suffix is kept only as a cross-check that must equal the resolved primary suffix; a mismatch fails setup. container-tag.test.sh gains structure checks for the suffix wiring and fixture cases for C++ (clang-20), TypeScript (node-24), Python with a matching caller suffix, and three mismatched-suffix failures. Ref #1020

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: <ul> <li>derive single-container job image suffixes from the resolver (#1034) ci-quality's common job and ci-version-bump's version-bump job built their image suffix from the caller's container-suffix (else base), so a C++ or TypeScript caller passing no suffix ran on prod-base, and a Java or Rust caller on the unpublished prod-base:. Both setup jobs now run the primary-suffix action on the shared setup action's primary-version and container-suffixes, and the jobs run on prod-:, the image CI's primary leg uses (clang-20 -> prod-cpp-clang:20). The caller's container-suffix stays a must-match cross-check. The action now serves CI and CD, so it moves from actions/cd/release/primary-suffix to actions/shared/setup/primary-suffix; cd-release, its harness and the docs follow with unchanged behaviour. The new image.test.sh harness, run from smoke-setup-vergil, checks the wiring of all three single-container jobs, that no workflow job builds its image from inputs.container-suffix or inputs.language, the resolved images for C++, TypeScript, Python and no-language fixtures, and loud failure on mismatched caller suffixes. docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • build every package cell on the matrix-recorded runtime and check it before signing (#1038) cd-release's package-build and ci-package's build pass each cell's matrix-recorded runtime to vrg-package build --runtime, through matrix.runtime || '' so a non-python cell passes an empty value, never null. package-sign now checks out the repo, installs vergil-tooling, downloads the package-manifest artifact and runs vrg-package check-runtime on the unsigned packages after rpm is installed and before signing, so a mixed-runtime release stops before anything is signed or tagged. Adds the package-runtime.test.sh harness to the cd-release smoke workflow and documents the runtime on the cd-release and ci-package pages. Needs vergil-tooling 2.1.262 (v2.1). Ref #1029

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: <ul> <li>match uv commands with global options in the uv pin guard (#1055) The uv pin guard in pin-python/tests/pin.test.sh matched only 'uv ', so a global option before the subcommand (uv --quiet run, uv -q sync, uv --directory d run) hid the command from both the UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system check and the detect.sh --no-config check. Both regexes now allow any run of global options (each optionally with one value) before the subcommand, and accept --no-config among the global options or among the bare flags right after the subcommand. uv tool, uv --version, comments and backtick prose stay exempt. Adds 13 fixtures both ways; no existing case changes result.

docs.text:
• deploy un-versioned site when versioning-scheme=none (#714) Docs repos with versioning-scheme=none (single-branch org docs sites) were still deployed through mike, producing a versioned site: a 'dev' version with the current content plus an init '0.1'/'latest' version frozen at scaffold. The root redirected to /dev/, but /latest/ (and /0.1/) served stale content, and the /dev/ URL prefix and version selector are meaningless for a repo with one branch and no versions.

Read versioning-scheme from vergil.toml (same [project] read used for primary-language). When it is 'none', skip mike entirely and publish a single plain site to the gh-pages root via 'mkdocs gh-deploy --force' — no version split, no versions.json, no selector. --force replaces the branch, so the prior dev/0.1/latest fragments are cleaned up on the next deploy. Versioned repos are unchanged.

docs.text:
• name release job "release / release" to match confirm-main gate (#720) vergil-tooling's confirm-main stage (hardened under #1853) matches the CD release job name EXACTLY against "release / release" and fails closed on any other name. This repo runs a reduced inline release job (freeze-refs + tag-and-release; no registry publish, as an actions-only library) whose display name was "cd / release" — a designed convention (see the CD-checks table in the 2026-05-09 workflow-convention spec, where CD checks were informational, not enforced).

The floating v2.1 tooling pin adopted the tightened gate silently between the 2.1.5 release (passed) and 2.1.6 (stalled at confirm-main, leaving a half-applied release and open tracking issue #715).
