docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add reusable cd-docs-refresh workflow (#726) Org documentation-site repos publish generated roadmap/activity pages that change with epic activity, not with any release of the docs repo — so there is no push or release event to rebuild on. They need a scheduled + on-demand job that regenerates the pages and republishes the site.

Add cd-docs-refresh.yml, a reusable workflow that wraps cd-docs.yml with the page generation pre-wired as its pre-deploy-command default (vrg-roadmap / vrg-activity-log). Every org's docs repo drives it from a thin caller (on: schedule + workflow_dispatch), rather than duplicating the generation command. Reusing cd-docs.yml inherits the full deploy path, including the un-versioned single-site deploy from #713.

docs.title: Chores
docs.text: • ignore .vergil/ tooling scratch dir (#731) The .vergil/ scratch dir (pr-workflow.json, vrg-validate/finalize logs) was untracked and unignored here, so every worktree read dirty via git status --porcelain. That tripped the removable gate in vrg-worktree-status and vrg-finalize-pr, leaving merged worktrees unreapable. Aligns vergil-actions with the rest of the fleet, which already ignores it. Ref #730.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add reusable ops-epic-rollup workflow (#733) Add ops-epic-rollup.yml, a reusable workflow that runs vrg-epic-rollup for a just-closed task's parent epic. Fires via a thin on: issues.closed caller (per repo convention), mirroring the ops-github-config App-token pattern.

Parameterizes the epic repo (default .github) and the App token so it works across all three orgs: the token is scoped to the caller repo plus the epic repo, and each org's caller passes its own APP_CLIENT_ID / APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets. The cross-repo epic close stays our code, not a keyword, since epics live in a different repo than tasks.

Part of epic vergil-project/.github#75. Refs vergil-project/vergil-tooling#2042 (vrg-epic-rollup CLI), vergil-project/vergil-tooling#2052 (thin caller).

docs.title: Reusable Workflows
docs.text: v2.0.0 introduced reusable CI workflows that provide canonical job and check names across all managed repositories. Each workflow bundles one or more composite actions with the container, tooling, and permission setup needed to run them. CD workflows handle post-merge delivery (releases, documentation).

docs.title: Why reusable workflows?
docs.text: Composite actions run as steps within a caller-defined job. Reusable workflows run as complete jobs, which means they control the job name that appears in GitHub's checks UI. This guarantees consistent, canonical check names across repositories — a requirement for pattern-based required status checks in rulesets.

docs.title: CI workflows (pre-merge)
docs.text: Workflow File Purpose CI Docs ci-docs.yml Build-only MkDocs strict verification (no deploy) CI Security ci-security.yml Security scanning (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep) CI Quality ci-quality.yml Common linting, custom validation, language-specific lint and typecheck CI Audit ci-audit.yml Dependency audit CI Test ci-test.yml Unit tests CI Version Bump ci-version-bump.yml Version divergence gate CI Package ci-package.yml Build and install-test .deb/.rpm packages (repos with [package] only)

docs.title: CD workflows (post-merge)
docs.text: Workflow File Purpose CD Release cd-release.yml Full release pipeline (tag, build, publish, version bump); repos with [package] also build, sign and attach .deb/.rpm packages (binary packages) CD Docs cd-docs.yml MkDocs documentation deployment Publish package index publish-index.yml Signed apt/dnf package-repository site, deployed to Pages CD Docs Refresh cd-docs-refresh.yml Regenerate the roadmap and activity pages and redeploy the docs site, on a schedule

docs.title: Ops workflows (scheduled and event-driven)
docs.text: Workflow File Purpose Ops GitHub Config ops-github-config.yml Nightly vrg-github-repo-config audit, branch sweep, and vrg-dependabot-audit open-alert gate Ops Epic Rollup ops-epic-rollup.yml Close a task's parent epic when its last task closes (called on issues: closed) Ops Epic Sweep ops-epic-sweep.yml Daily org-wide reconciliation: close epics and tasks that missed their event-driven close, drain standing epics into archives, and attach orphan issues to an epic Ops Upstream Refresh ops-upstream-refresh.yml Scheduled vrg-upstream-refresh: run the repository's [upstream-refresh].hook, then open or refresh one human-merged PR, or close a stale one when nothing changed

docs.title: Dynamic version matrix and evidence gates
docs.text:
The matrixed CI workflows (ci-audit, ci-quality, ci-test) take their version matrix from vrg-ci-resolve at run time, via the shared setup action's outputs. The resolver reads the consumer's vergil.toml and the published language version window: a library builds the whole window, any other repository type builds one version, and a [ci].versions pin must lie inside the window. Each leg asserts that it runs the version it was resolved for (ci/toolchain/assert). A consumer's ci.yml is therefore a thin caller that passes only language: and container-suffix:. The versions: and container-tag: inputs were removed in #899.

Single-container jobs (ci-quality's common and custom, ci-version-bump, and cd-release's release) run on the resolver's primary version: [ci].primary-version if set, else the newest resolved version, on the resolver's image suffix and tag for it (clang-20 runs on prod-cpp-clang:20; see shared/setup/primary-suffix). The caller's container-suffix never picks an image: the matrix legs accept any resolved suffix as a cross-check, and the single-container jobs require the primary version's.

Each matrixed workflow emits a stable, version-agnostic aggregate gate named <kind> / evidence — audit / evidence, quality / evidence, and test / evidence. The evidence job needs every matrix leg and runs with if: always(), asserting each leg's result is success, so a failed or skipped leg makes the aggregate fail red rather than skip green. Branch protection requires these stable evidence gates, not the per-version legs, so the required-check set does not churn when the resolved version set changes (a new language window, or a change to the [ci].versions pin). See Required Checks.

quality / evidence always bundles the common job's transcript (quality-common.log, the full vrg-validate --check common output) alongside any lint/typecheck reports. That transcript gives a language-less repo (container-suffix: base), which has no lint/typecheck reports, a real quality report. Release-time harvest rejects an evidence.json-only payload as incomplete, and cd-release follows each evidence step with an explicit enforcement guard, so an incomplete gate blocks the release in enforcing mode (see All Hard Gates).

quality / evidence also bundles the custom job's transcript (quality-custom.log, the full vrg-validate --check custom output). The custom job runs the repo's custom validator (scripts/bin/validate-custom or vrg-validate-custom) in PR CI, or logs one "no custom validator" line and passes when the repo has none. The evidence job needs it, so a failed or skipped custom stage fails quality / evidence — no extra required check (epic vergil-project/.github#488).

docs.title: Consuming a reusable workflow
docs.text:
Reference workflows using the full path to the workflow file with a rolling minor tag pin:

uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1

Tag pinning

The same tag pinning guidance applies as for composite actions. Pin to @v2.1 for automatic patch releases, or @v2.1.0 for full reproducibility.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Reusable workflows inherit permissions from the calling workflow. Callers must declare the permissions each workflow needs at the job level:

jobs:
  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: python

A called workflow's own permissions: blocks are requests against the caller: GitHub validates at workflow startup that the calling job's effective permissions cover every requested scope, and rejects the run with startup_failure if they do not. See each workflow's page for the scopes it requests.

docs.title: Container image prefix
docs.text:
All reusable workflows run inside container images from the ghcr.io/vergil-project/ registry. The image name follows the pattern:

ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>

The prefix defaults to prod and selects which image variant to use. Every reusable workflow accepts a container-prefix input that overrides this default. The Docker images are part of the development and deployment environment only — there is no runtime dependency on them from the artifacts these workflows produce.

docs.title: Overriding the prefix
docs.text:
To test against development Docker images, pass container-prefix: dev to the reusable workflow calls in the consumer's ci.yml, cd.yml, or ops.yml. Override a single workflow call to test one phase, or override all calls in a file to run the full CI/CD pipeline against dev images.

Single workflow override:

jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python
      container-prefix: dev

Full CI file override (add container-prefix: dev to every call):

jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python
      container-prefix: dev

  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-prefix: dev

  test:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-test.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python
      container-prefix: dev

Committing and pushing the overrides is expected when running a full end-to-end integration test of the dev images through CI and CD. Remove the overrides once the dev images have been validated and promoted to prod.

For local validation using development containers, see the vrg-container-run documentation for instructions on specifying the container prefix.

docs.title: Reference freezing
docs.text: The workflow source files reference composite actions via @develop during development. At release time, the publish workflow freezes all @develop references to the release tag (e.g., @v2.1.0), ensuring that a pinned workflow version uses the matching action versions.

docs.title: cd-docs-refresh
docs.text:
Regenerates a docs site's generated pages and republishes the site. It is a thin wrapper over cd-docs.yml with the page generation pre-wired.

It exists for an organization's documentation-site repository, whose roadmap and activity pages change with epic activity in the org rather than with any change to the docs repository. There is no push or release to rebuild on, so the caller runs it on a schedule and on demand.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description pre-deploy-command string no vrg-roadmap > docs/site/docs/roadmap.md && vrg-activity-log > docs/site/docs/activity.md Command that regenerates the generated pages before the deploy mkdocs-config string no docs/site/mkdocs.yml Path to the MkDocs configuration file container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description refresh <caller> / refresh / docs Calls cd-docs.yml, whose docs job runs the command, stages the docs and deploys them

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The refresh job calls cd-docs.yml with the three inputs. Its docs job:

  1. Checks out the repository with full history and installs vergil-tooling.
  2. Runs pre-deploy-command. The default runs vrg-roadmap and vrg-activity-log, which read the org's .github epics with gh; the step sets GH_TOKEN to the workflow's github.token, which is enough because the epic home is public.
  3. Stages the changelog and release notes with shared/docs/stage.
  4. Deploys with cd/docs/deploy: mike for a versioned site, or mkdocs gh-deploy to the gh-pages root for a repository with versioning-scheme = none.

cd-docs runs in the cd-docs concurrency group without cancelling, so a refresh queues behind a deploy that is already running.

The nested call is to cd-docs.yml@develop, fully qualified so it resolves when cd-docs-refresh is called from another repository. The release freezes that ref to the release tag (see Reference freezing).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents write The deploy pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
name: CD Docs Refresh

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  refresh:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-docs-refresh.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: write

The Run workflow button (workflow_dispatch) is the manual "refresh now".

docs.title: cd-release: binary packages
docs.text:
When the caller's vergil.toml has a [package] section, cd-release.yml also builds, signs and attaches the repo's .deb/.rpm packages:

Job Behavior package-matrix Always runs. vrg-package check-unpublished --version <version> first refuses the release if any package it would publish (same name, full version, arch and format) was already published by an earlier release; a repo without [package] passes. Then vrg-package matrix --github-output --manifest packages-manifest.json resolves the build cells and writes the release manifest. For each builder = "python" package it resolves the vergil-python runtime once, and records it as runtime on that package's build cells and in the manifest's runtimes map. With several [[package]] entries, cell ids are package-qualified (<name>--<id>). package-build / <cell> One job per build cell, on the cell's runner inside its build OS image, with the same toolchain as ci-package.yml. It runs vrg-package build --cell <cell> --runtime <runtime> with the cell's recorded runtime, so every cell of a package builds on the same runtime. A cell without one (a non-python builder) passes an empty --runtime, never null. The packages are unsigned. package-sign Declares the package-signing environment. Before signing anything it runs vrg-package check-runtime --manifest packages-manifest.json --artifacts dist/packages, which fails unless every .deb and .rpm of each python package depends on exactly the runtime the manifest records for that package (packages with no recorded runtime are not checked). It then signs every .rpm with the org signing subkey and verifies each signature, then attests the provenance of every package. release Runs only if package-sign succeeded. It attaches the signed packages and packages-manifest.json to the Release, then dispatches package-released to <owner>/packages.

A re-published package version, a failed build cell, a mixed-runtime package set or a failed signing step stops release before anything is published or tagged. The runtime check (vergil-tooling#3478) catches cells that built on different runtimes, as vergil-tooling 2.1.258 did (amd64 on vergil-python3.15, arm64 on vergil-python3.14). The --runtime and check-runtime options need vergil-tooling 2.1.262 or later at the caller's [dependencies].vergil pin; v2.1 resolves to it. The re-publish check is the CD backstop for a release that did not go through vrg-release preflight, which runs the same check: a package version published twice breaks the shared package index for every repo. Any gh error fails the check rather than skipping it. The dispatch is deferred: if minting the App token or the dispatch fails, the release still stands. The index's weekly reconcile picks it up, and vrg-release reports the miss. Repos without [package] see only the extra package-matrix job. The other package jobs are skipped, and they never reference the package-signing environment.

A packaged repo needs:

  • A package-signing environment. Its deployment-branch policy must admit only main. It holds the PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY secret (the ASCII-armored export of the signing subkey) and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE. If the key is missing or empty, package-sign fails.
  • secrets: inherit on the caller (required). Environment secrets reach a job in a cross-repo reusable workflow only when the caller passes secrets: inherit. An explicit secrets: map, or passing nothing, delivers an empty value; declaring the secret in the callee makes no difference (verified by a controlled probe, vergil-project/packages#6). Semgrep's secrets-inherit rule flags this, so suppress it on that line with a justification (# nosemgrep: …; honored by the SARIF gate since vergil-project/vergil-tooling#3107). inherit also forwards the org App secrets APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY, which the index dispatch needs. The App must be installed on <owner>/packages with permission to create repository dispatches (contents: write).
  • The same permissions the release job already needs. The package jobs request only contents: read, id-token: write and attestations: write:
jobs:
  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: python
    # Required: environment secrets only reach the reusable workflow with inherit.
    secrets: inherit  # nosemgrep: yaml.github-actions.security.secrets-inherit.secrets-inherit

docs.title: cd-release
docs.text: The release pipeline. On a push to main it checks the CI evidence of the release PR, builds and publishes the release, tags it and creates the GitHub Release. Repos with [package] in vergil.toml also build, sign and attach .deb/.rpm packages (binary packages).

docs.title: Container image
docs.text:
The release job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>:

  • <prefix> is container-prefix (default prod).
  • <suffix> and <tag> are the resolver's image suffix and tag for the primary version ([ci].primary-version, or the newest resolved version), the same image CI's primary leg runs on. The setup job runs the shared setup action, which calls vrg-ci-resolve against the consumer's vergil.toml and the published language version window. The tag is its primary-container-tag; the suffix is the primary version's entry in its container-suffixes, picked by shared/setup/primary-suffix.

For example clang-20 gives prod-cpp-clang:20, node-24 gives prod-ts-node:24, 3.14 gives prod-python:3.14 and a language-less repo's latest gives prod-base:latest.

So a release builds and tests on the image CI resolves today, not on a tag written into the caller's cd.yml when the repo was initialized, or a suffix guessed from language (language: cpp used to name prod-cpp, which is not published). The caller passes no tag, and needs no container-suffix. If it passes one, the value must equal the resolved suffix, or setup fails: the caller's cd.yml and vergil.toml disagree on the language. A resolver error fails setup too, and release does not run.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Default Description language string "" Language ecosystem (go, java, python, rust). Omit it for repos with no language. container-suffix string "" Cross-check only. The image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must equal the resolved primary suffix (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or setup fails. It never changes the image. container-tag string "" Deprecated and ignored. The tag comes from the resolver. A non-empty value only adds a ::warning:: to the run. The input is kept for one release so callers that still pass it do not fail: GitHub rejects a reusable-workflow call that passes an input the workflow does not declare. It is deleted once vergil-tooling#3484 removes it from every caller. container-prefix string prod Image name prefix (prod or dev). registry-publish boolean false Publish build artifacts to the language's package registry. build-command string "" Override the ecosystem's build command. publish-command string "" Override the ecosystem's publish command. attestation-subject-path string "" Glob for build provenance attestation. Empty skips it. sbom-output-file string "" SBOM output path ($VERSION placeholder). Empty skips it. release-artifacts string "" Files to attach to the Release ($VERSION placeholder). evidence-enforce boolean true true fails the release before publish when the CI evidence is incomplete or failed. false only warns, as a temporary per-repo opt-out.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text: Job Behavior setup Always runs. Resolves primary-container-suffix and primary-container-tag for release, fails if the caller's container-suffix disagrees with the resolved suffix, and warns if the caller passed container-tag. package-matrix Always runs. Resolves the package build cells; a repo without [package] reports none. See binary packages. package-build / <cell>, package-sign Packaged repos only. Every cell builds on the runtime package-matrix recorded, and package-sign checks every package against it before signing. See binary packages. release Runs when setup and package-matrix succeeded, and package-sign too for a packaged repo. Validates the inputs, gates on the CI evidence, publishes, tags and releases, then attaches the evidence bundle.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      registry-publish: true

The caller's permissions: must include actions: read (the evidence gate downloads the release PR's CI evidence artifacts), contents: write, id-token: write and attestations: write. A packaged repo must pass secrets: inherit; see binary packages.

docs.title: ci-audit
docs.text: Dependency audit workflow.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. Each leg's image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must be one of the resolved suffixes (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or the matrix job fails. It never changes an image. container-prefix string no prod Image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Secret Required Description CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER no ConanCenter provider token for conan audit. Only meaningful for cpp repos; other ecosystems ignore it. Pass it explicitly via the caller's secrets: block — never secrets: inherit. When unset, the cpp audit command skips the conan gate with a notice instead of failing auth.

docs.title: Version matrix
docs.text: The matrix comes from vrg-ci-resolve at run time: the workflow's matrix job runs the shared setup action, which calls the resolver, and passes its versions, image tags and image suffixes to ci/matrix. Each leg pins uv to its version and to the image's interpreter (Python, with ci/toolchain/pin-python) and then asserts the running toolchain with ci/toolchain/assert. Callers are thin: they pass only language: and container-suffix:.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description dependencies / <version> <caller> / dependencies / <version> Dependency audit (matrix-expanded — informational, not a required check) evidence audit / evidence Aggregate gate — needs every dependencies leg, runs if: always(), and asserts each leg succeeded; a failed/skipped leg makes it fail red rather than skip. This stable, version-agnostic gate is the required check (see Required Checks)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  audit:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-audit.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

For cpp repos, forward the ConanCenter provider token through the explicit-secret chain so conan audit can authenticate:

jobs:
  audit:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-audit.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: cpp
      container-suffix: cpp-clang
    secrets:
      CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER: ${{ secrets.CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER }}

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: The dependencies job provides a version matrix scaffold for running language-specific dependency audit tools (e.g., pip-audit, npm audit, bundler-audit).

docs.title: ci-docs
docs.text: Build-only documentation verification workflow. Runs the same staging as the CD docs deploy and then mkdocs build --strict — without mike, a push, or any credentials — so documentation that fails to build is caught at PR time instead of post-merge in the CD docs deploy.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description mkdocs-config string no docs/site/mkdocs.yml Path to the mkdocs configuration file container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text:
Job Check name Description build <caller> / docs Stages docs sources and runs a strict mkdocs build

With the standard caller job key docs, the check is docs / docs, which is a required check for repositories that publish docs (see Required Checks).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The build job:

  1. Checks out the repository with full history (fetch-depth: 0) so the changelog and release-notes staging can read tags.
  2. Detects whether the configured mkdocs config exists. When it is absent the remaining steps are skipped and the job passes — repos without docs are unaffected, mirroring how cd-docs is wired in only for repos that publish documentation.
  3. Stages changelog and release-notes pages and patches the mkdocs nav using the shared actions/shared/docs/stage action — the same staging the CD docs deploy performs, so a green CI docs check reliably predicts a green CD docs deploy.
  4. Runs mkdocs build --strict. The build is credential-free (no mike, no --push, no id-token); --strict turns nav and reference warnings into failures.

For Python repositories the build runs as uv run mkdocs; otherwise it runs mkdocs directly, matching the toolchain resolution in actions/cd/docs/deploy.

docs.title: Interpreter source
docs.text:
The build job sets UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system in its job env, so every uv command in the job, including uv run mkdocs, uses the image's Python (/usr/local/bin/python3 in prod-base). A repository may set uv's python-preference (for example only-managed). Without the pin, uv would download a managed Python for the docs build, or fail when the repository also sets python-downloads = "manual". uv's environment variables take precedence over a repository's uv settings (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec §6.5).

Only the source is pinned. The job resolves no Python version, so UV_PYTHON is not set and uv picks the image's interpreter against the repository's requires-python. If the image cannot satisfy it, the build fails loudly. There is no fallback. Repositories that do not set these uv options build as before. Added in issue #1002.

docs.title: MkDocs 2.0 banner
docs.text: The "Build docs" step sets NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING=1. Without it, mkdocs-material 9.7.x prints a MkDocs 2.0 warning banner on every build. The workflow has to set the variable itself: a caller's env does not reach a reusable workflow, so callers cannot set it. The variable only hides the banner. Consumers still pin mkdocs<2 in their own docs dependencies. Added in v2.1.43 (#947, PR #948).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  docs:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-docs.yml@v2.1

Add the job only in repositories that publish documentation ([publish] docs = true in vergil.toml), the same condition under which cd-docs is wired into cd.yml.

docs.title: ci-package
docs.text: Build and install-test a repo's binary OS packages (.deb/.rpm) from its [package] section.

docs.title: Tiered matrix
docs.text:
ci-package.yml is called only by repos whose vergil.toml has a [package] section. Calling it without one fails the run. Its gate job surfaces as package / evidence under a caller job keyed package.

The matrix job picks a tier and passes it to vrg-package matrix --github-output --tier <tier>:

Event Tier Pull request from release/* into main full Any other pull request reduced Any non-PR event (push, workflow_dispatch, …) full

The reduced tier keeps every build cell but runs only one install-test leg per format, so feature PRs get feedback sooner. For each format it picks from that format's shared (non-native) targets, or from its native ones if it has no shared target. It prefers amd64 (falling back to arm64) and takes the oldest release, compared numerically: the strictest compatibility case (lowest glibc, oldest rpm/dnf/systemd). The selection is done by vergil-tooling's vrg-package matrix (lib/package/matrix.py).

Release PRs always run the full tier, and the release evidence harvest reads the release PR's CI. A caller can override the automatic choice with the optional package-tier input (auto, full or reduced; default auto). Any other value fails the matrix job.

jobs:
  package:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-package.yml@v2.1
    with:
      package-tier: full  # optional; omit for auto

package / evidence runs in both tiers. It fails unless the matrix, build and install-test jobs all succeeded, and it records the tier that ran as metrics.tier in the ci-evidence-package artifact.

This needs a vergil-tooling release whose vrg-package matrix accepts --tier.

docs.title: Build runtime
docs.text: For builder = "python", vrg-package matrix resolves the vergil-python runtime once and records it as runtime on every build cell (vergil-tooling#3478). Each build / <cell> job passes it on as vrg-package build --cell <cell> --runtime <runtime>, as cd-release.yml's package-build does, so PR builds and release builds use the same runtime on every architecture. A cell without a runtime (a non-python builder) passes an empty --runtime, never null, which vrg-package build reads as none recorded. This needs vergil-tooling 2.1.262 or later at the caller's [dependencies].vergil pin; v2.1 resolves to it.

docs.title: Toolchain setup
docs.text:
Each build / <cell> and install-test / <cell> job runs inside the cell's OS image and sets it up with package/setup. On x86_64 Ubuntu images that action points apt at a mirror list, as GitHub's hosted runners do: the Azure mirror first, then archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com as fallbacks. On every apt image it writes a fail-fast apt config (3 undelayed retries, 20-second timeouts, a 60-second dpkg lock wait) that all later apt calls in the job inherit, and it runs a single apt-get update. arm64 cells keep ports.ubuntu.com. UBI cells install through one bounded dnf call.

Every package job sets timeout-minutes, in both ci-package.yml (matrix 5, build 30, install-test 15, evidence 5) and cd-release.yml (package-matrix 5, package-build 30, package-sign 15). A normal build takes about 45 seconds, so a stall fails the job in minutes rather than running to GitHub's 6-hour limit.

docs.title: ci-quality
docs.text: Code quality, linting and custom validation workflow.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. Every image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must equal the primary version's resolved suffix (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or setup fails. It never changes an image.

docs.title: Version matrix
docs.text: The lint and typecheck matrix comes from vrg-ci-resolve at run time: the workflow's matrix job runs the shared setup action, which calls the resolver, and passes its versions, image tags and image suffixes to ci/matrix. Each leg pins uv to its version and to the image's interpreter (Python, with ci/toolchain/pin-python) and then asserts the running toolchain with ci/toolchain/assert. The single-container common and custom jobs run on the resolver's image for the primary version (see Common checks and Custom validation). Callers are thin: they pass only language:, and optionally container-suffix: as a cross-check.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description common <caller> / common Runs common linters based on file presence (single-container job on the primary version — informational, gated through quality / evidence) custom <caller> / custom Runs the repo's custom validator with vrg-validate --check custom, or logs that there is none (single-container job on the primary version — informational, gated through quality / evidence) lint / <version> <caller> / lint / <version> Language-specific linting (matrix-expanded — informational, not a required check) typecheck / <version> <caller> / typecheck / <version> Language-specific type checking (matrix-expanded — informational, not a required check) evidence quality / evidence Aggregate gate — needs the common, custom, lint, and typecheck jobs, runs if: always(), and asserts each succeeded; a failed/skipped leg makes it fail red rather than skip. This stable, version-agnostic gate is the required check (see Required Checks)

docs.title: Common checks
docs.text:
The common job runs inside a single container on the primary version — ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>, the image the primary lint and typecheck legs run on. The setup job resolves both parts with the shared setup action: <tag> is its primary-container-tag, and <suffix> is the primary version's entry in its container-suffixes, picked by shared/setup/primary-suffix. For example clang-20 gives prod-cpp-clang:20, 3.14 gives prod-python:3.14 and a language-less repo's latest gives prod-base:latest. If the caller passes a container-suffix that differs from <suffix>, setup fails and common does not run.

The job conditionally executes each linter based on whether matching files exist in the repository:

Tool Condition markdownlint *.md files found shellcheck *.sh files or scripts/bin/ directory found yamllint *.yml or *.yaml files found hadolint Dockerfile* files found actionlint .github/workflows/ directory found

docs.title: Custom validation
docs.text:
The custom job runs the repository's custom validator (scripts/bin/validate-custom or vrg-validate-custom) in PR CI with vrg-validate --check custom, which runs the language install stage and then the custom stage. A repository with no custom validator gets one "no custom validator" line and a passing job; a validator that is present but not an executable regular file fails the job. Like common, it runs once, on the same image. For Python it pins uv to the primary version's interpreter (with ci/toolchain/pin-python) and installs the dev dependency group first, so the validator sees the repo's dev dependencies; ci/toolchain/assert then checks the running toolchain is the primary version.

The job's transcript is uploaded as the ci-evidence-quality-reports-custom partial and bundled into ci-evidence-quality as quality-custom.log. The evidence job needs custom, so a failed or skipped custom stage fails quality / evidence — there is no separate required check (epic vergil-project/.github#488).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: The lint and typecheck jobs provide a version matrix scaffold. Consuming repositories customize these jobs by forking the workflow or by running language-specific tooling in a separate workflow that calls these as a baseline.

docs.title: ci-security
docs.text: Security scanning workflow: CodeQL, Trivy and Semgrep, plus an evidence job that bundles their SARIF results for the release harvester.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Language for the security scanners (e.g., python, go, java) run-security boolean no true Run the scanner jobs (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep) run-codeql boolean no true Run CodeQL analysis (disable for languages CodeQL does not support, such as shell) upload-sarif boolean no true Upload scanner SARIF to GitHub code scanning (disable on private repos without GHAS; see below) container-prefix string no prod Image name prefix (prod or dev) for the semgrep job's <prefix>-base:latest container run-standards boolean no false Deprecated — no longer has any effect. The standards job it controlled was removed; the input is still accepted so consumers that pass it do not error container-suffix string no — Deprecated — fed the removed standards job and no longer has any effect. Still accepted so consumers that pass it do not error

New callers should not pass run-standards or container-suffix.

docs.title: Required permissions
docs.text:
permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write
  actions: read

actions: read is required by codeql-action/upload-sarif on private repositories (it reads the workflow run via the Actions API). Public repositories do not need it, but reusable-workflow jobs can only downgrade caller permissions, so the caller must grant it for the workflow-level grant to take effect.

docs.title: Upgrading from v2.1.2 or earlier
docs.text:
v2.1.3 added actions: read to this workflow's permissions: request. GitHub validates the request against the calling job's effective permissions at startup, so a caller whose security: job carries an explicit permissions: block (the standard posture) must add actions: read to that job-level block — the job block fully replaces any workflow-level block in the caller, so a workflow-level grant alone is not sufficient. Callers without the grant fail with startup_failure and no registered checks.

The grant is backward-compatible with earlier releases, so it can merge before the workflow pin moves to v2.1.3. See #698 for the incident that motivated this note.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text:
GitHub names each check <caller job> / <job>. With the caller job keyed security (the standard posture, as in the usage examples below):

Job Check name Condition codeql security / codeql run-security, run-codeql, and upload-sarif are all true trivy security / trivy run-security is true semgrep security / semgrep run-security is true evidence security / evidence trivy and semgrep succeeded, and codeql succeeded or was skipped

The evidence job downloads each scanner's SARIF partial and emits the consolidated ci-evidence-security artifact. If any scanner fails, it does not run, so no security evidence is emitted. It is not a required check; see Required Checks for which of these checks branch protection requires.

When SARIF is uploaded to code scanning, GitHub also adds its own SARIF analysis checks (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep OSS); see Security Scanning.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: python

To skip CodeQL for languages it does not support:

jobs:
  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: shell
      run-codeql: false

docs.title: Private repos without GitHub Advanced Security
docs.text:
GitHub code scanning on private repositories requires GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS). On a private repo without GHAS, set upload-sarif: false:

jobs:
  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: python
      upload-sarif: false

With upload-sarif: false:

  • Trivy and Semgrep scans still run and still fail the job on findings; their SARIF results are attached to the workflow run as build artifacts (trivy-fs-sarif, semgrep-sarif) instead of being uploaded to code scanning.
  • The codeql job is skipped entirely — CodeQL cannot run on private repos without GHAS, regardless of the upload destination.

The scans themselves do not require GHAS; only the code-scanning upload destination does. Failing CI because the reporting destination is unavailable, when the scan itself passed, is the wrong outcome — this input degrades the destination, not the scanning.

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
• The semgrep job runs inside the ghcr.io/vergil-project/<container-prefix>-base:latest container (prod-base by default). Semgrep never executes the target code, so it needs no language runtime.
  • The codeql and trivy jobs run directly on ubuntu-latest, with no container. CodeQL autobuild for compiled languages needs the language toolchains that the runner provides.
  • Each scanner job uploads its unfiltered SARIF as an evidence partial regardless of upload-sarif. For Trivy and Semgrep, the copy sent to code scanning omits accepted-suppressed results (via vrg-sarif-filter); the evidence copy keeps them so they remain auditable.
  • The Semgrep action auto-detects repository content and enables additional rulesets: p/dockerfile when Dockerfiles are present, p/github-actions when workflow files exist under .github/workflows/. No configuration is needed from consuming repos. For cpp the workflow adds p/c (which covers .c files only), and for typescript it adds p/typescript.

docs.title: ci-test
docs.text: Unit test workflow.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. Each leg's image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must be one of the resolved suffixes (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or the matrix job fails. It never changes an image. container-prefix string no prod Image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Version matrix
docs.text: The matrix comes from vrg-ci-resolve at run time: the workflow's matrix job runs the shared setup action, which calls the resolver, and passes its versions, image tags and image suffixes to ci/matrix. Each leg pins uv to its version and to the image's interpreter (Python, with ci/toolchain/pin-python) and then asserts the running toolchain with ci/toolchain/assert. Callers are thin: they pass only language: and container-suffix:.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Condition unit / <version> <caller> / unit / <version> Matrix-expanded per version — informational, not a required check evidence test / evidence Aggregate gate — needs every unit leg, runs if: always(), and asserts each leg succeeded; a failed/skipped leg makes it fail red rather than skip. This stable, version-agnostic gate is the required check (see Required Checks)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  test:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-test.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

docs.title: System packages
docs.text:
Each unit job installs the system packages the repository declares under [container].system-packages in its vergil.toml, via the shared/setup/system-packages action. This runs on test jobs only — lint and typecheck jobs do not exercise the code and are deliberately excluded, so the packages are installed exactly where the tests need them and nowhere else.

The install is a no-op when a repository declares no system packages. When it does declare them, the step installs with a bounded retry (to absorb transient apt mirror flakes) and fails closed if a declared package has no install candidate — the offending package and platform are named in the log and the test job fails rather than running against a missing dependency. See the action reference for the full behavior, and the container-config reference on the vergil-tooling side for the [container].system-packages key itself.

docs.title: Build command
docs.text:
After the system-packages install, each unit job runs the command the repository declares under [container].build-command in its vergil.toml, via the shared/setup/build-command action. Like the system-packages install, this runs on test jobs only — lint and typecheck jobs do not exercise the code and are deliberately excluded — and it runs after the packages are installed, before the tests.

The step is a no-op when a repository declares no build command. When it does declare one, the step fails closed with no retry: an arbitrary build command that fails is a real failure, not a transient one, so — in deliberate contrast to the system-packages install's bounded retry — a non-zero exit fails the test job immediately rather than being retried and masking a genuine break.

After the command runs, the action exports NODE_PATH (the npm global root, from npm root -g) so subsequent test steps can resolve a node library the build baked out-of-workspace (e.g. npm install -g <lib>).

require-only caveat. NODE_PATH is honoured by CommonJS require resolution only; ESM import ignores it. A baked library consumed via import will not resolve through NODE_PATH — a documented Node limitation, not an action bug.

See the action reference for the full behavior, and the container-config reference on the vergil-tooling side for the [container].build-command key itself.

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: The unit job provides a version matrix scaffold. Consuming repositories customize it by forking the workflow or by running language-specific test commands in a separate workflow.

docs.title: ci-version-bump
docs.text:
Version divergence gate workflow.

The gate follows the consuming repo's configuration: the job reads release-model from vergil.toml and, when it is "none", passes without running the gate. Non-releasing repos need no caller wiring to stay green.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository run-release boolean no true Deprecated — the gate follows release-model in vergil.toml. Passing false still suppresses the gate but emits a deprecation warning. Tracked for removal in #688 container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. The image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must equal the primary version's resolved suffix (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or setup fails. It never changes the image.

docs.title: Image
docs.text: The version-bump job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>, the resolver's image for the primary version, as in ci-quality's common job: <tag> is the shared setup action's primary-container-tag, and <suffix> is the primary version's entry in its container-suffixes, picked by shared/setup/primary-suffix (clang-20 gives prod-cpp-clang:20, a language-less repo gives prod-base:latest).

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text:
Job Check name Condition setup <caller> / setup Always runs; resolves the image suffix and tag for version-bump, and fails if the caller's container-suffix disagrees with the resolved suffix version-bump <caller> / version-bump Always runs; the gate steps run only when release-model is not none

With the standard caller job key version (as in the usage example below), the required check is version / version-bump, for repositories whose release-model is not none.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  version:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-version-bump.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python

Repos that don't release (e.g., infrastructure or documentation repos) declare it in vergil.toml instead of passing run-release: false:

[project]
release-model = "none"

The version-bump job then passes without running the gate, and the tooling-derived required-check set omits it entirely.

docs.title: ops-epic-rollup
docs.text:
Event-driven epic rollup. When an issue closes, it runs vrg-epic-rollup, which closes the issue's parent epic once every task in that epic is closed.

The rollup is a no-op unless the closed issue is a managed task whose parent is a finite epic (an epic-labelled issue that is not a standing ad-hoc epic), so the caller can run it on every issue close. Epics usually live in a different repository (the org's .github), which is why the workflow uses a GitHub App token rather than GITHUB_TOKEN.

ops-epic-sweep is the scheduled safety net for any close this workflow misses.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev) epic-repo string no .github Repository in the caller's org that holds the epics. The App token is scoped to it so the rollup can close the parent epic there

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's GitHub App APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's GitHub App

The App must be installed on the calling repository and on epic-repo, with issues: write.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description epic-rollup <caller> / epic-rollup Runs vrg-epic-rollup for the closed issue

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The epic-rollup job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-base:latest:

  1. Mints an App token scoped to the calling repository and epic-repo.
  2. Checks out the repository and installs vergil-tooling.
  3. Runs vrg-epic-rollup --task "<owner>/<repo>#<issue number>" with the App token as GH_TOKEN.

The issue number comes from github.event.issue.number, so the caller must be triggered by an issues event.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout. Issue writes use the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
name: Epic Rollup

on:
  issues:
    types: [closed]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  epic-rollup:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-epic-rollup.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

docs.title: This repository's caller: epic-rollup
docs.text: .github/workflows/epic-rollup.yml in this repository is exactly the caller above: it runs on issues: closed and passes the App secrets to ops-epic-rollup.yml@v2.1. It is not a reusable workflow. Each managed repository carries the same thin caller, and all the logic (token, checkout, install, run) stays in ops-epic-rollup.

docs.title: ops-epic-sweep
docs.text:
Scheduled epic and task reconciliation. It runs vrg-epic-audit --close, which makes three passes over the whole org:

  • Drift close. Closes work that missed its event-driven close, for example when the ops-epic-rollup run failed, a secret was broken or two closes raced: epics whose tasks are all closed, and task issues whose PR has merged. It also reopens an epic that was closed while a child was still open.
  • Archive drain. Moves the closed children of every standing epic (ad-hoc, intake and planning) into per-quarter archive epics.
  • Orphan pass. Enforces "every issue belongs to an epic": it links body-only Parent: lines as native sub-issues, removes the retired triage, idea and research labels, moves a now-public repository's self-homed intake and planning items under the org .github queues, and attaches every orphan to its home's intake epic.

So the sweep changes labels and sub-issue links, not only issue state. Each pass acts only on provable drift, so a run with nothing new to fix changes nothing.

The org's epic home calls it once a day; one run covers the whole org. The same caller's workflow_dispatch trigger is how the one-time migration for "every issue belongs to an epic" is run.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev) window-days string no "30" How many days back to look for merged PRs whose task issue is still open. Epic drift (all tasks closed) is not limited by the window

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's GitHub App APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's GitHub App

The token is minted for every repository the App is installed on in the org, because the sweep closes, relabels, links and moves issues in the code repositories, and closes, drains and attaches under epics in .github. The App needs issues: write on all of them.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description epic-sweep <caller> / epic-sweep Runs vrg-epic-audit --close across the org

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The epic-sweep job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-base:latest:

  1. Mints an App token for the caller's org, with no repository restriction.
  2. Checks out the repository and installs vergil-tooling.
  3. Runs vrg-epic-audit --close --window-days "$WINDOW_DAYS" with the App token as GH_TOKEN and VRG_EPIC_SWEEP=1.

vrg-epic-audit --close runs its passes in this order:

  1. Closes drifted tasks and rolled-up epics, and reopens any epic closed with an open child.
  2. Drains the ad-hoc epics, then the intake and planning epics, into per-quarter archives, and closes past archives.
  3. Runs the orphan pass: links body-only Parent: lines natively, strips the retired labels, moves now-public repositories' queue items under .github (closing each emptied self-homed queue epic), then attaches orphans to intake.

The log prints a count line for each step, for example Retired kind labels stripped: 41 issue(s). and Orphans attached to intake: 50.

docs.title: When a run fails because a queue is full
docs.text:
An intake or planning epic holds at most 95 open children. When an epic is at that cap, the orphan pass stops before it adds anything past it. The step prints every issue it did not link and exits 1, so the run fails. A failed run can therefore mean the queue needs attention (run intake review, or work the planning queue), not only a broken token or an outage. The next run attaches the rest once the queue has room.

vrg-epic-audit --close is otherwise a human-only action: it refuses unless the identity resolves to human. VRG_EPIC_SWEEP=1 marks this scheduled run as the trusted automation that may close. An interactive agent session never sets it.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout. Issue writes use the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
name: Epic Sweep

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  epic-sweep:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-epic-sweep.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

docs.title: ops-github-config
docs.text:
Nightly per-repository ops checks. Every managed repository's ops.yml calls this workflow on a schedule, and it runs three independent jobs against the calling repository:

  • branch-sweep deletes branches whose pull-request work is finished.
  • github-config audits the repository's GitHub configuration with vrg-github-repo-config audit.
  • dependabot-audit fails when the repository has any open Dependabot alert, at any severity.

The jobs do not depend on each other, so one failing does not stop the others. Each one mints its own GitHub App token from the org's automation App (see APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY), scoped to the calling repository only.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's automation GitHub App (<org>-automation) APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's automation GitHub App

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description branch-sweep <caller> / branch-sweep Deletes finished branches via ops/github-config/branch-sweep github-config <caller> / github-config Runs vrg-github-repo-config audit --repo <calling repo> dependabot-audit <caller> / dependabot-audit Runs vrg-dependabot-audit --repo <calling repo>

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Every job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-base:latest and follows the same pattern:

  1. Mints an App token with actions/create-github-app-token. None of the jobs passes an owner or repositories input, so each token is scoped to the calling repository alone.
  2. Checks out the repository and installs vergil-tooling.
  3. Runs its command with the App token as GH_TOKEN.

docs.title: Token permissions per job
docs.text:
Job Requested App permissions Why branch-sweep contents: write, pull-requests: read Delete a branch ref, and read pull requests to decide which branches are finished github-config None requested, so the token carries the installation's full permission set (still limited to the calling repository) The audit reads repository settings, branch protection, rulesets, Actions permissions, whether vulnerability alerts are enabled, and the repository's vergil.toml and CI workflow dependabot-audit vulnerability-alerts: read only (Dependabot alerts: Read) List the repository's open Dependabot alerts

GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do this work. This workflow requests only contents: read for it, and a called workflow can never hold more than its caller's ops.yml grants (the standard ops.yml grants contents: read and issues: write). Neither can delete a branch or read Dependabot alerts.

The audit is read-only, and the App's Administration permission is Read-only to match. vrg-github-repo-config apply, which changes settings and rulesets, is a human action run under the maintainer's own gh login, never by this workflow.

docs.title: branch-sweep
docs.text: The scheduled safety net behind the delete-on-merge repository setting and the delete-on-close rule. It lives in this workflow so that every repository whose ops.yml already calls it is swept with no consumer change. See ops/github-config/branch-sweep for what is deleted, the job summary and the failure handling.

docs.title: github-config
docs.text: Runs vrg-github-repo-config audit --repo "${{ github.repository }}", which compares the repository's live GitHub configuration with the expected configuration and exits non-zero when they differ or the configuration cannot be read. It never changes anything. To converge a repository, a human runs vrg-github-repo-config apply (see Repository Rulesets).

docs.title: dependabot-audit
docs.text:
The fleet runs Dependabot report-only (epic vergil-project/.github#420): alerts are on, Dependabot never opens a pull request, and this job turns any open alert into a red nightly run. It runs vrg-dependabot-audit --repo "${{ github.repository }}". Dismissing an alert on GitHub is the only way to clear it.

The exit codes are a contract:

Exit Meaning Job result 0 No open alerts Pass 1 At least one open alert, at any severity Fail 2 The alerts could not be read: alerts disabled, the token lacks Dependabot alerts: Read, no App installation, or an unknown repository Fail

"Could not check" (exit 2) is never treated as a pass. A common cause is an App permission change that has not yet been accepted on the org's installation: until it is, minted tokens do not carry the new permission. See Changing a permission later.

A private repository's log carries an itemized report. A public repository, or one whose visibility cannot be resolved, gets counts by severity and a link to the Security tab only, so a world-readable log never names a vulnerable package.

For the command's full reference, see vergil-tooling's Dependabot Alert Audit.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout. Every other operation uses the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The standard ops.yml, as generated by vergil-tooling's vrg-github-repo-init (which staggers the cron minute per repository):

name: Ops

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '45 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  github-config:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-github-config.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

docs.title: ops-upstream-refresh
docs.text:
Scheduled upstream refresh. It runs vrg-upstream-refresh, which runs the calling repository's [upstream-refresh].hook from vergil.toml and turns the result into at most one pull request:

  • No change. The run exits quietly. If a refresh PR is still open, it is closed with a comment and its branch is deleted, because the base branch already has the change or it no longer applies.
  • A change. The change is committed to the fixed upstream-refresh branch, which is force-pushed only when its content differs, and one PR is opened or refreshed with the hook's notes in its body. Superseded refresh PRs are closed.

The workflow never merges. The PR's own CI checks it, and a human reviews and merges it. An upstream refresh is separate from a dependency update: vrg-upstream-refresh never runs the [dependency-update] hook, and vrg-update-deps never runs the [upstream-refresh] hook. See the vergil-tooling upstream-refresh configuration reference for the hook contract.

Each consumer calls it from its own ops.yml on its own schedule.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's GitHub App APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's GitHub App

The token is scoped to the calling repository only. The App needs contents: write (to push and delete the upstream-refresh branch) and pull-requests: write (to open, update, comment on and close the refresh PR) on that repository.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description upstream-refresh <caller> / upstream-refresh Runs vrg-upstream-refresh against the branch the run is on

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The upstream-refresh job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/prod-base:latest, in the concurrency group upstream-refresh (a new run waits for a running one; neither is cancelled):

  1. Mints an App token scoped to the calling repository.
  2. Checks out the repository with that token, so the push and the PR are App-authored. An App-authored PR triggers pull_request workflows, which a GITHUB_TOKEN push does not.
  3. Marks the workspace safe for git and sets the git identity to github-actions[bot].
  4. Installs vergil-tooling at the caller's [dependencies].vergil ref.
  5. Runs vrg-upstream-refresh --base "$BASE" with the App token as GH_TOKEN. BASE is the branch the run is on (github.ref_name), passed through the environment.

A failed run (a hook that exits non-zero, or leaves untracked files behind) shows as a red scheduled run.

vrg-upstream-refresh refuses the agent identity modes (user and audit), because it opens PRs. This workflow sets no agent identity; its GitHub writes are made with the App token.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read A called workflow cannot exceed its caller's grant. The push and PR writes use the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
name: Ops

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  upstream-refresh:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-upstream-refresh.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

Schedule it on the default branch, so BASE is that branch.

docs.title: publish-index
docs.text: publish-index.yml is called from an <org>/packages repository. Its build-index job runs vrg-package index --config packages.toml --keys keys --out _site, which verifies, retains, indexes and signs the product releases. Its deploy job then publishes the site with the Actions-based Pages deploy. The workflow takes no inputs. Runs are serialized by the publish-index concurrency group. Unlike the other reusable workflows, it runs directly on ubuntu-latest rather than in a vergil container image.

docs.title: Attestation verification
docs.text: Before indexing, vrg-package index verifies every downloaded .deb and .rpm with gh attestation verify, pinned to the signer workflow vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml and the source ref refs/heads/main. An asset whose build provenance was not attested by cd-release.yml running on a product's main branch fails the index build. Each .rpm's org signature is checked as well.

docs.title: Caller requirements
docs.text:
• Pages source set to "GitHub Actions". The deploy job publishes with actions/deploy-pages, so the caller repository's Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source must be GitHub Actions, not "Deploy from a branch".
  • An index-signing environment (below).
  • secrets: inherit and the job permissions shown in the example.

docs.title: Signing environment and caller example
docs.text:
The signing key comes from the caller repository's index-signing environment, which must admit only develop and hold PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE. As with cd-release, those environment secrets reach the reusable workflow only when the caller passes secrets: inherit (see cd-release: binary packages). The caller must also grant the scopes the two jobs request:

jobs:
  publish-index:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/publish-index.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    # Required: environment secrets only reach the reusable workflow with inherit.
    secrets: inherit  # nosemgrep: yaml.github-actions.security.secrets-inherit.secrets-inherit
